title: Solana Apps Generate $193M in 30 Days Amid Real-World Assets Surge
summary: Solana generated $193.1 million in application revenue over the past 30 days, nearly twice Hyperliquid’s total, according to Castle Labs research. content:
Solana generated $193.1 million in application revenue over the past 30 days, nearly twice Hyperliquid’s total, according to Castle Labs research. More importantly, the network’s growth is spreading beyond meme coins, with real-world assets surging from $700 million to $4.37 billion in a year.

Key Takeaways

  • Solana apps generated $193.1M in 30 days, nearly 2x Hyperliquid’s $86.5M.
  • RWAs grew 600% from $700M to $4.37B in the last year, showing growth beyond meme coins.
  • The next phase depends on whether RWA and lending growth can make revenues more durable.

Solana RWAs Surge to $4.37B as Growth Moves Beyond Meme coins

Solana has become crypto’s highest-grossing application ecosystem, and the numbers suggest its revenue engine is becoming broader than the meme coin boom that helped build it.

Applications on Solana generated $193.1 million in revenue over the past 30 days, according to Castle Labs. Hyperliquid ranked second with $86.5 million, followed by Ethereum at $53.8 million and Robinhood-related activity at $34.6 million.

Roughly 80% of Solana’s app revenue still comes from consumer applications such as launchpads, trading terminals, and collectibles. But the research argues that this revenue is proving more durable than critics assume.

Meme Coins Built the Revenue Engine

Pump.fun remains the standout business. The launchpad generated about $39 million in trailing 30-day revenue, equal to roughly 20% of all Solana application revenue. Its Pumpswap exchange added another $15 million.

Yet Solana’s consumer economy is becoming less concentrated.

Weekly consumer-app revenue ranged from $13.5 million to $42.6 million over the past year, with a median of $18.2 million. Eight of the 10 largest apps from late 2025 remained in the top 10 by the third quarter of 2026.

Meanwhile, the top three applications’ share of consumer revenue fell from 64% to 50.2%, suggesting newer products are taking meaningful market share.

RWAs Are Becoming Solana’s Second Growth Story

The bigger structural shift is happening in tokenized real-world assets.

Solana’s RWA market value climbed more than 600% in one year, from roughly $700 million to $4.37 billion. Ethereum, by comparison, grew from $15.5 billion to $16.6 billion over the same period.

Tokenized stocks on Solana jumped from $63 million to $455 million, driven by platforms including xStocks and Backpack.

More than $65 million of tokenized equities are already being used to earn yield, while broader active RWA value in Solana DeFi exceeds $500 million, about 8% of the network’s net value locked.

Solana Is Testing Whether Growth Can Outlast Speculation

That is the part worth watching.

Solana still depends heavily on speculative consumer activity. But Castle Labs’ data suggests the ecosystem is adding lending, tokenized credit, equities, and yield-bearing assets around that core.

The investment case is therefore changing.

Solana’s next phase will not be judged only by how many meme coins launch. It will be judged by whether those consumer revenues can coexist with deeper lending markets and productive RWAs.

If that happens, $193 million in monthly app revenue may look less like a cycle peak and more like a base.

Are crypto sign-up bonuses worth it?

You see, no-deposit bonus offers are rare, and a free crypto sign-up bonus with instant withdrawal usually comes with a lock, KYC step, or trading condition. The better way is to value a bonus at what you can personally use. Also, most of the bonus funds usually arrive as trading credit or vouchers rather than withdrawable cash. Which crypto exchange sign-up bonus is the best for your trading type?

High-Frequency and Grid Traders

Here, fee rebates, futures credits, trading vouchers, and volume-based rewards become more valuable because you naturally place many trades. Are free crypto sign-up bonuses available for every exchange?

Basically, each platform decides its own promotion rules, and some exchanges do not offer any reward just for creating an account.

Even exchanges that advertise a welcome bonus usually ask you to complete certain steps first. So, you may need to verify your identity, deposit a minimum amount, make your first trade, or reach a required trading volume. The reward can also vary by country, campaign period, and referral link.

Can I withdraw my free crypto bonuses immediately?

No, you cannot withdraw a free crypto bonus immediately, as most exchanges place conditions on the reward because the bonus is meant to encourage real trading activity, not simply give away withdrawable cash.

You should also check the exchange app terms carefully, since bonuses can vary by region and some platforms use promotions to grow their user base.

You may need to deposit funds, complete KYC, make a certain number of trades, or reach a required trading volume before the bonus even becomes eligible for withdrawal. Plus, some rewards cannot be withdrawn at all. Of course, this works differently from exchange to exchange. Hence, you should always check the withdrawal terms first, especially the minimum trading requirement, expiry date, and whether the bonus itself or only the profits can be withdrawn.

title: Claude AI Cracks the NSA’s 25-Year Cryptography Seed Mystery
summary: For 25 years, cryptographers suspected the NSA’s mysterious encryption seeds might conceal a backdoor. Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence (AI) cracked the puzzle in under 30 minutes, uncovering a surprisingly ordinary explanation. For decades, some of the world’s brightest cryptographers had...
content:
For 25 years, cryptographers suspected the NSA’s mysterious encryption seeds might conceal a backdoor. Anthropic’s Claude artificial intelligence (AI) cracked the puzzle in under 30 minutes, uncovering a surprisingly ordinary explanation.

Key Takeaways

  • Anthropic says Claude solved a 25-year NSA encryption mystery in under 30 minutes.
  • NIST’s five prime-field curve seeds trace to a Unix-era generator using 1997-98 timestamps.
  • Anthropic’s $36,864 bounty went to ISRG, while the origin of the B-163 seed remains unresolved.

For decades, some of the world’s brightest cryptographers had been chasing a ghost. Five mathematical curves used to protect internet communications carried mysterious numbers supplied by the National Security Agency (NSA), and nobody could satisfactorily explain where those numbers came from. Theories ranged from forgotten jokes to deliberately planted weaknesses. Then Anthropic’s Claude AI took a crack at the puzzle and traced the numbers to an old computer program and timestamps dating back nearly three decades.

A 25-Year Mystery With the NSA at Its Center

The story begins in the late 1990s, when mathematicians were developing standards for elliptic curve cryptography, a method of protecting digital information using sophisticated mathematics. Five curves, known as P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521, eventually became part of standards published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Their mathematics helped secure websites, financial transactions and government communications.

But here’s the kicker. Each curve had been constructed using a mysterious 160-bit starting number called a seed. Anyone could verify the mathematical procedure used to produce the curves, but nobody knew how the NSA had chosen those original numbers. That unanswered question fueled speculation that the agency might have deliberately selected seeds to conceal a weakness only its own specialists could exploit.

Cryptographers Neal Koblitz and Alfred Menezes examined the controversy in their 2015 paper, “A Riddle Wrapped in an Enigma.” No practical backdoor was ever demonstrated, but the mystery refused to die.

The Secret Phrase That Apparently Never Existed

For years, the prevailing explanation involved NSA mathematician Jerry Solinas, who reportedly supplied the original seeds. Solinas and others recalled that the numbers had been generated by hashing humorous English phrases, possibly something resembling “Jerry deserves a raise.” Hashing converts information into a fixed-length mathematical fingerprint. Unfortunately, nobody remembered the exact phrases, and the original computer had reportedly been replaced.

Solinas himself tried reconstructing the process without success. The mystery eventually acquired a price tag. In October 2023, cryptographer Filippo Valsorda offered a $12,288 bounty for anyone who could explain the seeds’ origins. A charitable matching arrangement brought the potential payout to $36,864. For three years, the money went unclaimed. Then Claude entered the picture.

Claude Finds the Answer Hiding in Plain Sight

According to Anthropic’s research published Oct. 16, an employee asked an internal Claude research model to investigate the seeds without mentioning the longstanding secret-phrase theory. The model began examining patterns associated with older computer programs. One clue immediately stood out. Several seeds contained groups of numbers whose highest bits were consistently zero, a pattern with roughly a 1-in-5,810 chance of appearing randomly.

That pointed toward lrand48, a pseudorandom number generator commonly available in Unix-era programming environments. Unlike genuinely random processes, pseudorandom generators produce predictable sequences once their starting values are known. Claude worked backward through the mathematics, recovered the generator’s internal states and reproduced the published seeds exactly. Then came the real humdinger.

The starting values corresponded to Unix timestamps, ordinary numerical representations of dates and times, from 1997 and 1998. The model’s recorded reasoning captured its own apparent disbelief. “This is astonishing: it solves the 25-year-old mystery.” The whole business took less than 30 minutes.

Five Curves, Five Timestamps and One Extraordinary Match

The recovered starting values traced the five NIST prime-field curves to specific dates between May 1997 and April 1998. P-192 originated from a timestamp corresponding to May 18, 1997, while P-521 traced to Aug. 8 of that year. P-256 followed on Aug. 16, P-384 on Aug. 30, and P-224 on April 3, 1998. The apparent recipe was almost comically simple. Initialize an ordinary random-number generator with a timestamp, produce candidate seeds, test them against mathematical requirements and keep searching until an acceptable curve emerges.

Here’s a video explaining it: https://t.co/BEC7wJ641p

— Steve Weis (@sweis) October 16, 2026

For P-256, the accepted seed appeared at candidate 1,842. For P-224, it took 7,026 candidates. The matches were exact, reproducing all 160 bits of the published seeds rather than merely producing similar-looking numbers. Valsorda independently reproduced the results using the Go programming language, confirming the findings. Anthropic also released code allowing others to check the work. The results provide strong mathematical evidence for the generation method, although they don’t establish precisely who operated the original software or why certain candidates were rejected.

What the Discovery Means for Internet Security

The implications are reassuring, though they don’t amount to a universal security guarantee. One longstanding concern involved the possibility that the NSA possessed enough freedom when selecting seeds to deliberately choose mathematically vulnerable curves. The recovered process appears to have offered far fewer choices than some hypothetical attacks would require. Anthropic’s researchers estimated roughly 30 bits of selection freedom under generous assumptions, considerably less than the approximately 70 bits contemplated in one proposed weakness-selection scenario.

That makes this particular backdoor theory substantially less plausible. Importantly, the discovery doesn’t break elliptic curve cryptography or establish that every possible weakness has been ruled out. It also doesn’t directly affect Bitcoin or Ethereum, which use a different elliptic curve called secp256k1.

Gregory Maxwell Throws Cold Water on Claude’s Big Moment

Interestingly, Bitcoin developer Gregory Maxwell offered a less enthusiastic take, claiming on Hackernews that he had suggested investigating the same cryptographic mystery on Sept. 20 to a friend with expiring Anthropic AI credits. The friend’s AI agent spent hours on the problem without success, leaving Maxwell unimpressed with its reasoning abilities.

Maxwell, an outspoken critic of Anthropic’s approach to AI, questioned whether the company had restricted his friend’s model capabilities and poked fun at the publicity surrounding Claude’s discovery. He stopped short of claiming credit or disputing the findings, suggesting the difference in results might simply reflect how the AI was directed.

“I’m not saying this to suggest that misanthropic hijacked someone elses work yet again– this is an obvious question that many people have surely posed and success presumably depended on expert use (which was absolutely not applied in my friends example),” Maxwell wrote. “But it does make me wonder if the company invisibly degraded the model performance.”

The Bounty Gets Paid, but Questions Remain

The discovery finally settled Valsorda’s three-year-old challenge. Anthropic’s team directed the $36,864 bounty to the Internet Security Research Group, which operates Let’s Encrypt. Valsorda described the finding as something that “helps fill out a page of cryptographic history, and reinforces our confidence in these critical cryptographic primitives.” A few loose ends remain. Researchers haven’t fully explained why some mathematically acceptable candidates were discarded, and the origin of another curve’s seed, B-163, remains unresolved.

Still, the central mystery appears solved. After decades of suspicion, speculation and failed attempts to reconstruct a supposedly forgotten secret phrase, the answer was sitting inside an ordinary 1990s computer routine. The NSA’s mysterious numbers weren’t necessarily hiding an elaborate secret. They may simply have been keeping time.

title: Wall Street Veterans Unveil DeFi Platform for 77 TradFi Markets
summary: Decentralized perpetual futures exchange Deepsigma has launched a live paper-trading platform across 77 traditional financial markets, including U.S. equities, indexes, commodities, and Treasury yields. Bridging Traditional Finance and Onchain Markets Decentralized perpetual futures exchange Deepsig...
content:
Decentralized perpetual futures exchange Deepsigma has launched a live paper-trading platform across 77 traditional financial markets, including U.S. equities, indexes, commodities, and Treasury yields.

Key Takeaways

  • Deepsigma unveiled a live paper-trading demo covering 77 traditional financial markets on Cypherium.
  • Former Goldman Sachs and Google alumni are expanding crypto perpetual models to traditional assets.
  • Deepsigma plans to deploy zero-knowledge proof identity tools to meet global regulatory standards.

Bridging Traditional Finance and Onchain Markets

Decentralized perpetual futures exchange Deepsigma recently unveiled its platform with a live paper-trading demo spanning 77 traditional financial markets. Developed by a team of alumni from Goldman Sachs, Citadel Securities, Google, and Uber, the platform allows traders to gain long or short exposure to U.S. equities, stock indexes, sector ETFs, commodities, and Treasury yields.

Rather than tokenizing, taking custody of, or taking delivery of the underlying assets, Deepsigma’s perpetual contracts track prices through external market data feeds. Built on the Cypherium Layer 1 blockchain, the project aims to bring the perpetual futures model to conventional financial instruments.

Sky Guo, CEO of Deepsigma and founder of Cypherium, said traditional assets present unique operational challenges compared with cryptocurrencies, including non-24/7 trading hours, fragmented pricing, and specific regulatory requirements.

“Crypto has already demonstrated the demand for perpetual markets, but you cannot simply take the same model and put a stock or commodity ticker on it,” Guo said. “Real-world markets have different trading hours, liquidity conditions, pricing sources, and regulatory considerations. We started DeepSigma with those differences in mind.”

The paper-trading platform currently supports contracts covering benchmark stock indexes including the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, Nasdaq Composite, Russell 2000, and Cboe Volatility Index (VIX). It also supports contracts with commodities such as crude oil, gold, silver, natural gas, and copper.

Technical Infrastructure and Risk Management

To address off-hours price movements and liquidity lapses in traditional markets, Deepsigma’s risk engine incorporates multi-source external price feeds, mark-price mechanisms to deter short-term manipulation, circuit breakers, partial liquidations, and an insurance fund. The platform operates on a central limit order book model paired with a clearing layer for margin, collateral, and settlement.

The interface also features an offchain artificial intelligence (AI) analysis tool designed to generate strategy insights without execution authority over user funds. Unlike fully permissionless crypto venues, Deepsigma is designing its system around U.S. regulatory frameworks.

The exchange is developing a decentralized identity framework utilizing zero-knowledge proofs. Meanwhile, the underlying Cypherium blockchain utilizes a hybrid proof-of-work and Hotstuff Byzantine Fault Tolerant consensus mechanism, supported by four U.S. patents.

title: Solana Abruptly Postpones Shanghai Event as Registrations Quadruple
summary: The Solana Foundation stated that the Accelerate event was canceled due to a surge in registrations, with people overwhelming the designated venue. Nonetheless, social media reports indicate the presence of law enforcement at the venue, with attendees remaining left outside for hours.   Solana Accel...
content:
The Solana Foundation stated that the Accelerate event was canceled due to a surge in registrations, with people overwhelming the designated venue. Nonetheless, social media reports indicate the presence of law enforcement at the venue, with attendees remaining left outside for hours.

Key Takeaways

  • Solana’s Accelerate event in Shanghai was abruptly postponed after venue capacity was overwhelmed.
  • Police reportedly blocked access, raising concerns that China is enforcing its strict anti-crypto laws.
  • Publicity and high turnout might have led authorities to dismantle the event, enforcing China’s crypto ban.

Solana Accelerate Event Postponed in China, Reports Indicate Law Enforcement Presence at Venue

One of the largest events of the Solana community in China, the Accelerate convention, was postponed on October 16, with attendees speculating about the reasons for this move.

Social media reports indicate that attendees arrived at the designated venue in Shanghai only to be left waiting for over an hour to access the event, which was programmed to be held at the Shangri-La Hotel in Shanghai on October 16.

Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation, explained that due to the publicity linked to the convention, “event registrations quadrupled overnight, far exceeding the event cap we had registered with local authorities, and we had no way to prevent people from overwhelming the venue.”

Liu specified that the foundation postponed the event until it can “better accommodate the breadth and scale of our community,” and apologized to the attendees who traveled to be part of the experience.

Nonetheless, photos suggesting the presence of law enforcement offices and first-hand accounts of officials blocking access to the venue point to local authorities canceling the event due to its cryptocurrency links, even when no talk was directed at this topic per the Accelerate Shanghai program.

“Sad to see. Looks like they really didn’t know the local policies?” said Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, weighing in on the postponement, also hinting at the enforcement of China’s anti-crypto policies as the real reason behind postponing the convention.

Zhao also pointed out that this was not the first time the same convention has been targeted by local police. The 2025 Solana Accelerate Shenzhen event was also temporarily canceled due to public safety reasons, as a similar overcrowding situation unfolded.

Other Chinese crypto sources also pointed out that the heavy publicity surrounding the event and the promotion of an office established by the foundation gave it a high profile, with authorities stepping in to dismantle the event and enforce local crypto policies put in place since 2021 and recently reinforced by the People’s Bank of China (PBOC).

title: Poetic Justice: Scammer Lost $5M in Bitcoin After Being Targeted by Ledger Thieves
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Poetic Justice: Scammer Lost $5M in Bitcoin After Being Targeted by Ledger Thieves
Chainalysis has revealed that a victim of last week’s Ledger theft was a scammer themself. 
This post Poetic Justice: Scammer Lost $5M in Bitcoin After Being Targeted by Ledger Thieves first appeared...
content:
Call it poetic justice: one of the biggest victims of last week’s Ledger theft happened to be a scammer themself, according to blockchain analysts, and lost nearly $5 million in bitcoin. 

In a post Thursday, Chainalysis wrote that a crook lost 60 bitcoins worth about $4.8 million they’d stolen via a so-called task scam. 

According to Chainalysis, the address was linked with a con where people were paid to fake sales and reviews of real items. They were told to add their own money in order to get paid — and then stolen from. 

But the mastermind behind the task scam moved the stolen money to Ledger addresses which were then targeted by different scammers last week.

“On Sep 22, the person behind the scam moved the proceeds into three separate Ledger addresses,” Chainalysis said. “On Oct 9, thieves emptied all three. One transfer each, into the same wallet. The wallet is reported as stolen funds.”

Paris-based Ledger last week said it had started an investigation after customers in South East Asia reported they’d lost funds after buying from Malaysia-based reseller, CryptoBilis. 

Ledger has since said that the scam was a massive organized crime operation where a group installed implants into devices and put them back on the market. The implants could read users’ seed phrases so criminals could then drain wallets. 

Calling it one the most “sophisticated attacks” the digital asset industry has experienced, Ledger is yet to reveal how much money has been lost — but blockchain investigator Specter said $86 million had been drained. 

And the task scam conman, according to Chainalysis, was one of the victims.

Ledger has said that it is working with law enforcement to “follow the funds and dismantle the attackers’ infrastructure” and has made sure no other vendors have been targeted by scammers. 

CryptoBilis has stopped selling Ledger products, the company said. 

Criminals have targeted bitcoin hardware sellers this year, with a huge attack taking place in July on the popular Coldcard products. 

Crooks were able to steal close to $120 million in bitcoin from Coldcard users because the devices had a firmware bug which led to faulty seed generation, allowing hackers to guess investor seedphrases. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Visa Moves Massive Stablecoin Payments Pilot Into Production Phase
summary: The company has moved its initiative from pilot to commercial deployment in partnership with Inyo Global, a payments infrastructure firm, using its Visa Direct service. With this move, Inyo Global enables receiving and prefunding stablecoin payments across more than 180 countries. Visa Direct Stable...
content:
The company has moved its initiative from pilot to commercial deployment in partnership with Inyo Global, a payments infrastructure firm, using its Visa Direct service. With this move, Inyo Global enables receiving and prefunding stablecoin payments across more than 180 countries.

Key Takeaways

  • Visa partnered with Inyo Global to launch real-time USDC stablecoin payout funding in 180 countries.
  • The system lets institutions prefund cross-border payments 24/7, bypassing traditional banking hours.
  • The move follows a 15x surge in Visa’s stablecoin volume, reaching a $20 billion annual run rate.

Visa Direct Stablecoin Capabilities Go Into Production Phase

Visa has entered a new phase in its digital assets adoption, introducing stablecoin capabilities to institutional partners by moving its payments pilot into a production phase.

On Thursday, the company announced that it had reached a milestone in enabling stablecoin payments in real-world commercial applications, bringing its Visa Direct capabilities to market in partnership with Inyo Global, a Massachusetts-based payments infrastructure company.

Inyo Global would serve as a key middleman, allowing other companies to harness Visa Direct to prefund payouts 24/7 with USDC, manage liquidity more efficiently, and leverage Inyo’s rails to complete their operations.

As explained by Visa, Visa Direct enables fiat-to-stablecoin cross-border payments, with recipients receiving dollar-pegged assets in real time in markets where payment infrastructure lags, offering predictable settlement values even outside normal banking hours.

Global Head of Visa Direct Vira Platonova highlighted in a statement that the next chapter for stablecoins was adoption, and that the company had been working with several partners to explore seamless stablecoin integration in their money platforms.

“We’re now seeing those efforts translate into live implementations, helping businesses access more flexible and efficient ways to fund and move money globally through Visa Direct, starting with Inyo Global as our first enabler,” said Platonova.

The rollout will power cross-border payments in over 180 countries where Inyo Global operates.

Robson Dantas, chief product and technology officer and co-founder at Inyo Global, stressed that the implementation would let institutional customers test the advantages of using stablecoins for these tasks. “By integrating Visa Direct’s stablecoin-enabled prefunding into the Inyo platform, we’re giving the money transmitters, fintechs, and payment companies we serve a new way to fund their payouts, one that is available around the clock and runs through the same Inyo APIs they already use,” Dantas declared.

Visa has been approaching stablecoins for some time. It recently reported that stablecoin settlements on its network reached a $20 billion annualized run rate, a 15x increase from the levels registered a year before.

In September, the credit giant also completed its first stablecoin settlement with Lloyds Banking Group, receiving $750K in USDC from the bank in a seven-day pilot that operated when traditional banks are closed.

title: Best Time to Modernize Your Data Infrastructure: Before or After It Starts Failing?
summary: After a company has put in a new database and transferred the records, it will run the numbers to see how the performance is. On the face of it, there are no issues. But when the finance department gets to the revenue dashboard, they are met with the very same kind of discrepancies that were an issu...
content:
Skip to content

After a company has put in a new database and transferred the records, it will run the numbers to see how the performance is. On the face of it, there are no issues. But when the finance department gets to the revenue dashboard, they are met with the very same kind of discrepancies that were an issue with the old system.

One need only look at a calculation carried over in the migration for a likely culprit; perhaps some refunds have been put in the wrong reporting period, or an amended transaction has not made it to the warehouse. There is little point in having quick queries if the figures are off to begin with.

Such is what makes for hard choices on infrastructure. An investment is dictated by such considerations as the cost of maintenance, the accuracy of reports, how well the database performs and the work entailed in doing away with the systems in place.

Look at the Cloud Bill a Little Closer

It is not uncommon for a database bill to be the subject of much scrutiny, even if the cost is not in proportion to the volume of information on hand. With certain analytical databases, one is put to the charge for computing resources used by queries. A dashboard that has to make repeated passes over a huge transaction table in order to put a handful of monthly totals on screen can run up an unexpected tab, all the more so with multiple teams running like reports.

To put a finger on where the money is going, there are query histories to consult. One will see from execution plans any number of superfluous scans, joins that are anything but efficient or calculations done over and over by the system.

Before parting with funds for a new platform, there are three things to look at:

  • Queries that are reading too much data. See if a report is scanning a whole table when it could be making do with some aggregated numbers or a few records.
  • Processing that is being done again and again. There may be pipelines in separate departments or for different applications doing the same sort of extraction and transformation.
  • Data in storage for no good reason. Have a look at intermediate tables, duplicate exports and temporary datasets, bearing in mind what has to be retained.

Such an inquiry might result in a reworking of the partitioning or the way queries and processing are scheduled. Summary tables are an option for those figures that are in high demand, provided they are refreshed as they should be.

Then there is the matter of the platform itself. Any estimate worth having will factor in everything from support and engineering to put the move in place to the storage, transfers, and resources needed. Do not be misled by a low per gigabyte rate; it is no indication of what the final bill will be.

Follow a Refund Through the Reporting Process

When a customer puts in an order and later asks for his money back, the sales application will put down both. How it does so is a matter of the software in question. Some will have a refund transaction of its own; others alter the original order. Then there is the reporting pipeline: if it is only set to import finished sales and not any changes made after the fact, the figure for that refund will be tallied as revenue.

You can see the issue in other circumstances too, say with an accounting correction or a change to a product identifier, or when two customer accounts are merged. Move the records to a different database, and the calculation in the report will be no different.

Engineers have to trace the records from extraction on through to storage to get to the bottom of it. What is the source application doing to signal an update? Is a deletion noted? And will the reporting system put new values in place of the old ones?

For receiving such changes, some databases have change data capture; elsewhere an API or incremental export is used by the application. There are requirements to be met with each one for dealing with the odd interruption or a record gone missing, or having to run the process again.

As for the published numbers, it is up to finance to determine what bearing a correction has on them. The engineers may put the treatment in place once agreed upon, but the rules of reporting are a business concern.

What an Uptime Percentage Leaves Out

While one can make use of availability statistics, they do not tell the whole story when it comes to the hands-on work of putting an entire reporting environment back in order.

Then there is the matter of cost. An analysis of outages by the Uptime Institute for 2025 has some telling numbers: 57 per cent of those surveyed put the price tag on their last major outage at $100,000 or more, with a fifth or so saying they were out more than a million dollars. Such research into the sort of infrastructure outages that are commonplace is instructive in gauging the financial impact of any service disruption.

For recovery planning, there are two metrics to go by. The RTO, or recovery time objective, sets the limit on how long an interruption can be tolerated; the RPO defines what amount of data loss is acceptable in terms of time.

Demanding recovery point requirements might be satisfied through replication, but an inadvertent deletion will find its way to a replica as well, so having separate backups that are recoverable is a must.

It is not a question of simply restoring database files. One has to have applications with the proper permissions and connections, and the services they are reliant upon. To get the data back to where it should be, transaction logs could be called for.

An exercise in recovery ought to put these dependencies to the test in conditions that are representative. What is uncovered may show that the environment as it stands would be better served by a redesign or some alteration of backup procedures.

Moving Everything at Once Creates Its Own Problems

It is not uncommon for a number of disparate applications to draw on the very same database, each with its own agenda. One might have a dashboard that is content with periodic refreshes; another application in front of the customer will not tolerate anything but low query latency. Then there is financial reporting, which is beholden to precise decimal arithmetic and the need to replicate past calculations.

To put all these workloads under one roof is to invite a good deal of testing overhead. And should a deployment go awry, the impact is felt across more business functions than would otherwise be the case.

Before deciding what belongs in the migration, the team needs answers to three questions:

  • Where does the data go? Trace the applications, reports, exports, and external consumers connected to the database.
  • Which details matter to those consumers? Record expected field formats, calculations, update frequency, and treatment of historical information.
  • Who will verify the replacement? Assign responsibility for checking results and agree on acceptable discrepancies.

Application settings, query logs, scheduled tasks, and conversations with system owners can reveal dependencies missing from the documentation. Some workloads may be suitable for separate reporting pipelines, whereas others rely on shared transactions that complicate separation.

Record counts and checksums help detect certain transfer errors. Reports used by finance and operations also need reconciliation against agreed business rules.

Companies can involve external data engineering services in database engineering, ETL/ELT development, migration, and DataOps. The scope should establish who handles production access, reporting approval, and the removal of obsolete connections.

When the Existing Database Becomes Difficult to Defend

An unsupported database version deserves attention for reasons that have little to do with query speed.

Security vulnerabilities may remain unresolved after vendor maintenance ends. Driver compatibility, operating-system requirements, and application dependencies can further restrict the available options.

Assessing the exposure requires checking vendor support conditions, security obligations, and the feasibility of upgrading the existing installation.

Capacity can present a separate problem. Consistently high resource consumption, unacceptable latency under representative workloads, or availability requirements beyond the platform’s capabilities may justify replacement.

Even then, the workload deserves investigation. Poor query design can exhaust substantial computing resources. Additional hardware may increase the bill without addressing inefficient processing.

A proposed replacement should demonstrate how it will handle the requirements the current platform struggles to meet. Performance tests, recovery exercises, and compatibility checks provide a much firmer basis for investment than general dissatisfaction with ageing technology.

Put Both Options Into the Budget

The expense of moving databases extends beyond the replacement platform. Engineers must adapt applications, transfer and verify records, test dependent systems, and prepare staff for changes in reporting procedures.

Running both environments during validation adds another expense. Retiring the previous system requires its remaining consumers to be identified and disconnected.

Keeping the existing database also has a price, including support contracts, maintenance work, recurring reporting corrections, and measures needed to address known technical risks.

The financial assessment becomes easier to examine when costs are separated into three groups:

  • Routine operating costs: Infrastructure consumption, software support, monitoring, and maintenance.
  • Engineering work: Repairs and upgrades for the existing system, alongside development, migration, and testing expenses for the replacement.
  • Exposure to disruption: Documented security weaknesses, recovery limitations, and the potential financial consequences of unavailable services.

Estimates should reflect measured workloads and the organization’s actual requirements. Assumptions about processing demand, infrastructure consumption, and migration complexity deserve particular scrutiny.

A supported database that meets recovery and performance requirements may have considerable value left. Persistent security exposure, failed recovery objectives, or technical limitations affecting essential operations can make replacement a stronger investment.

The decision ultimately depends on what the business needs the data environment to deliver, which shortcomings have been demonstrated, and how the proposed work will address them. A credible budget should make those connections visible.

title: Pixagram Announces Free Account Creation for 250 New Users Daily Through 2026
summary: Panama City, Panama, October 16th, 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Panama City, Panama, October 16th, 2026, Chainwire

Panama City, Panama, October 15th, 2026, Chainwire

Pixagram announces free account creation for up to 250 new members daily through the end of 2026. Built on the standalone Layer-1 Pixa blockchain, Pixagram is an anti-hierarchy social network where every post, vote, and comment is recorded as a signed on-chain transaction, with no ads and no cryptocurrency purchase required to get started.

Pixagram will cover the 20 PIXA network fee for up to 250 new members daily through the end of 2026. New members can claim a free @username at Pixagram.com and join the platform’s on-chain community for creators.

► Quit Renting the Spotlight — Users can register at http://pixagram.com

An On-Chain Username and Wallet Address

Opening a Pixa chain account normally costs around 20 PIXA. Pixagram is covering this fee for up to 250 new members daily through the end of 2026.

  • Username and wallet address: Each @username serves as an on-chain wallet address, replacing a randomly generated string of characters with a recognizable handle.
  • Blockchain-based registration: Once registered on the blockchain, an @username remains associated with its on-chain record, subject to the network’s rules and technical conditions.
  • Phone verification and privacy: One-time phone verification helps limit bot abuse of the daily account offer. A public @username can separate a creator’s online identity from their legal name, although public blockchain records may limit privacy.

Not Really Anti-Social, Truly Anti-Hierarchy

Mainstream social media serves advertisers while gatekeepers decide who sees your work. Pixagram—alongside platforms like Hive and Mastodon—is a SIGMA platform built for creators who prefer agency over status games. Your posts, art, followers, and feeds live directly on-chain with nothing in between, allowing you to reach every follower automatically.

NFT Platform Storage and Artwork Permanence

On many NFT platforms, the token sits on-chain while the image lives on a cloud server or IPFS—meaning a token can easily outlive its art.

On Pixa, every artwork is stored directly on-chain inside its post as a lossless image. Compact pixel art lives permanently on the blockchain and renders up to 4K resolution as a painting, CRT filter, hexagonal shapes, or square pixels.

  • Zero upfront cost: Every new account receives a starter delegation of stake (Resource Credits fuel) to cover posting and voting from day one.
  • Build Mode Note: Direct on-chain art sales launch in 2027, so everything you publish today builds your permanent portfolio ahead of the marketplace release.

► Less Lurking. One Original Post. Start at Pixagram.com

Proof-of-Brain and Community Curation

Instead of relying on the computational process used in Proof-of-Work systems, Pixagram uses Proof-of-Brain, a mechanism that allocates rewards based on posting, commenting, and voting activity.

  • Community reward distribution: 70% of newly issued PIXA is allocated to community-voted content, with 60% distributed to authors and 40% to curators after seven days.
  • Staking and governance mechanisms: Authors can receive Pixa Power, which determines voting weight and supports governance participation, and Pixa Supra (PXS), a unit referenced by an oracle to a agnostic purchasing power index (without a fixed dollar value). Curators can also receive Pixa Power.

Censorship-Resistant by Design

Built on the Hive codebase with Steem lineage, the Pixa chain started from a clean genesis block with no airdrop and produces a block every three seconds. While an application interface can hide a post from its view, it can never erase the transaction record from the chain.

Furthermore, every artwork is checked for copies using PAPH-X (an open-source perceptual fingerprint for pixel art) and indexed by the Search V4 engine.

“The old internet wants you trapped in feed fog, renting reach from gatekeepers who track every click. Today information is king, and Pixagram operates outside that hierarchy… Don’t believe the hype. Create it.” — Matias Affolter, Co-Founder of Pixa

“The strongest rebellion is a working alternative. We’re covering the network fee for 250 new accounts a day so any creator can step into build mode at zero cost. Claim your permanent @username now—because once a handle is written to the chain, it’s gone forever.” — Mathiew Estepho, Co-Founder of Pixa

Pixagram Account Registration and Developer Resources

Pixagram offers fee coverage for up to 250 new accounts daily through the end of 2026. Eligible new members can register and claim an @username at Pixagram.com. Additional technical information is available in the developer documentation at pixa.org.

About Pixagram

Pixagram is an on-chain pixel art and blog network developed by Pixagram AG (Zug, Switzerland) and operated by Pixa Rex S.A. (Panama City, Panama).

title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Jumps 5.92% in Third-Largest Hike of 2026
summary: On Friday, at block height 971712, bitcoin mining grew considerably more demanding as the network’s latest difficulty adjustment climbed 5.92% to 140.58 trillion, marking its highest reading since March 5. Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Hits Seven-Month High After 5.92% Increase The network’s difficulty,...
content:
On Friday, at block height 971712, bitcoin mining grew considerably more demanding as the network’s latest difficulty adjustment climbed 5.92% to 140.58 trillion, marking its highest reading since March 5.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin mining just got a whole lot tougher, with difficulty climbing 5.92% to 140.58 trillion, its highest reading since March 5 and the third-largest increase of 2026.
  • Better mining revenue brought more computing power back into the competition, pushing Bitcoin’s hashrate above 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s), even as daily earnings have recently cooled.
  • Another sizable difficulty increase could be around the corner on Oct. 28, with early estimates pointing to a 14.24% jump, although there’s still plenty of time for that figure to change.

Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Hits Seven-Month High After 5.92% Increase

The network’s difficulty, basically how hard miners must work to find the next Bitcoin block, increased from 132.72 trillion to 140.58 trillion. It was the third-largest increase of the year and continued a recovery that began over the summer. Metrics show that Bitcoin has logged a total of 21 difficulty adjustments this year, with the latest being the 10th rise.

The increase coincided with bitcoin’s price spike, which led to better revenue for miners. On Sept. 16, the hashprice, which measures the estimated daily revenue generated by a single petahash per second (PH/s) of computing power, stood at $37.56 before climbing above $41 on two occasions over the past 30 days, including Oct. 2.

Bitcoin Hashrate Reclaims 1 ZH/s

For much of the past 30 days, mining revenue hovered between 6% and 9% above its Sept. 16 level, but by Friday, Oct. 16, the hashprice had retreated to $36.75 per petahash per second. The improved revenue environment encouraged greater miner participation, propelling Bitcoin’s total network hashrate back above 1,000 exahash per second (EH/s), equivalent to 1 zettahash per second (ZH/s).

This resurgence in computing power has driven mining difficulty higher, as an expanding hashrate generally accelerates block production, prompting an upward difficulty adjustment when the 2,016-block epoch concludes ahead of schedule. Conversely, a declining hashrate slows block production, leading to a downward adjustment in difficulty. At the time of writing, the hashrate is coasting along at 1024.96 EH/s with block times around 8 minutes 45 seconds.

If the next epoch is mined faster than usual, then the difficulty adjustment due on or around Oct. 28, 2026 is expected to see an estimated 14.24% rise. But with only a few dozen of the 2,016 blocks mined so far, that projection could very well change considerably.

title: BFFS26 Denver: Joseph Kelly on Bitcoin Custody and Credit; Alan Lane on Banking Lessons
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

BFFS26 Denver: Joseph Kelly on Bitcoin Custody and Credit; Alan Lane on Banking Lessons
CPAs, wealth advisors, and lenders gather in Denver for BFFS26, featuring Patrick Lowry on public-company Bitcoin treasury reserves and Wyoming Deputy Secretary of State Colin Crossman on regula...
content:
The Bitcoin for Financial Services Summit (BFFS26) returns to Denver October 20–22, 2026, bringing together CPAs, wealth advisors, attorneys, lenders, and finance leaders who are building Bitcoin into their practices. Now in its second year, the summit has grown to more than 30 sessions across two full program days, with a speaker lineup drawn from the firms defining Bitcoin custody, credit, and advisory.

Headlining the program are Joseph Kelly, CEO and co-founder of Unchained, who opens the summit with a keynote on custody, credit, and trust at scale; Alan Lane, former CEO of Silvergate Bank, on lessons for Bitcoin and banking; Patrick Lowry, CEO of Samara Asset Group, on holding Bitcoin as a public-company treasury reserve; and Colin Crossman, Wyoming’s Deputy Secretary of State, on the regulatory outlook for banks, exchanges, and advisors. Additional speakers include Kate Goldman of Anchorage Digital, Sam Baker of River, Eric Yakes of Epoch Ventures, Daniel Hillery of UTXO Management, Moish Peltz of Falcon Rappaport & Berkman, and CJ Konstantinos of Peoples Reserve.

Sessions focus on practical application: bringing Bitcoin into wealth planning and family offices, Bitcoin-backed lending and mortgages, treasury accounting and valuation, retirement and income planning, charitable giving strategies, mining as an asset class, and fiduciary duty when clients hold Bitcoin. Dedicated workshops will offer continuing education credit for financial advisors and CPAs.

“Last year proved that financial professionals want more than a Bitcoin primer. They want to know how to serve clients who already own it,” said Jordan Guess, CPA, co-host of the summit in a press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine. “This year’s program is built around the questions advisors and accountants are actually getting from clients, answered by the people building the infrastructure.”

The summit opens Tuesday, October 20, with the Better Money Invitational golf tournament at City Park Golf Course, hosted with Bitcoin Sports Network, followed by a welcome party at The Space sponsored by Falcon Rappaport & Berkman. Evening programming includes wine and whiskey tastings, and Thursday begins with an optional sunrise hike in the Rocky Mountains.

BFFS26 is co-hosted by Jordan Guess and Wyatt O’Rourke of BFFS Media, producers of the Bitcoin for Financial Services podcast. Sponsors include Unchained, Anchorage Digital, UTXO Management, River, SOUND HSA, SustainHash, and Stormrake.

Registration is open now at https://www.bffs.media/summit.

Media contact: Wyatt O’Rourke, [email protected]

title: FCA to Review Complex-Product Risk Tests as AI Erodes Client Screening
summary:
Retail investors once had to Google the answers to qualify for high-risk CFDs and complex derivatives; generative AI has turned passing those questionnaires into a one-click exercise. 
 Now, the UK Financial Conduct Authority is preparing to call time on the shortcut, launching a review into how onl...
content:
2026-10-16T21:42:18.687+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 19:42 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Online tests may show that clients can find the right answers, not that they understand the risks of a leveraged product.
  • Failing a test does not always block a trade: some clients can proceed after a warning.

Retail investors once had to Google the answers to qualify for high-risk CFDs and complex derivatives; generative AI has turned passing those questionnaires into a one-click exercise.

Now, the UK Financial Conduct Authority is preparing to call time on the shortcut, launching a review into how online brokers screen retail clients as chatbots erode the credibility of traditional risk tests.

The Test Does Not Apply to Every Brokerage Account

An FCA-regulated broker should assess clients’ appropriateness before selling them complex or high-risk products.

Depending on the rules and product structure, the assessment can cover CFDs, complex leveraged exchange-traded products, restricted mass-market investments and qualifying crypto assets.

Unlike suitability assessment, an appropriateness test does not determine whether an investment fits the client’s financial position, objectives or wider portfolio.

It asks whether the person understands what they are buying. In some cases, if a client fails the test, a broker can issue a warning and still allow the transaction if the client asks to continue.

Restricted mass-market investments face a higher threshold: the firm must assess the product as appropriate before accepting the order, with waiting periods applying after repeated failed attempts.

Why Passing a Test Does Not Prove Understanding

The regulator asked brokers and other stakeholders whether appropriateness tests still work for people investing without advice. Some of them warned that clients can use online searches and AI to find the right answers without understanding the risks.

In an online assessment, clients can look up answers as questions appear. Generative AI makes that easier than ever. Respondents to the FCA’s consultation warned that a passing score may therefore reflect someone’s ability to find information rather than their understanding of the investment.

This is especially dangerous with leveraged products. A client may correctly define margin even if they don’t understand how losses can grow when a position moves against them. An answer to an isolated question may not reveal that gap.

The test itself also varies between brokers. Firms have considerable freedom over its content: some assess clients’ understanding rigorously, while others treat it as a “tick-box exercise.”

They also differ over which instruments they consider “non-complex” and exempt from testing. Clients buying similar products may therefore face very different checks.

FCA Will Examine Alternatives in 2027

The FCA continues to view appropriateness assessments as an important safeguard and noted that only a small minority of respondents wanted them abolished or replaced.

Instead, the regulator plans to examine how the current model works, the harm created by its weaknesses and the merits of alternative approaches. It expects to begin engaging with brokers, consumer groups and other stakeholders in 2027.

The review may eventually change how brokers design and document their tests, but the FCA has not yet proposed a replacement model or set a timetable for new rules.

Until then, firms remain responsible for ensuring their questionnaires assess understanding rather than merely presenting another obstacle that clients, and now AI, can quickly navigate.

Instead, the regulator plans to examine how the current model works, the harm created by its weaknesses and the merits of alternative approaches. It expects to begin engaging with brokers, consumer groups and other stakeholders in 2027.

The review may eventually change how brokers design and document their tests, but the FCA has not yet proposed a replacement model or set a timetable for new rules.

Until then, firms remain responsible for ensuring their questionnaires assess understanding rather than merely presenting another obstacle that clients, and now AI, can quickly navigate.

title: Ethereum Founder Vitalik Buterin Details His ‘Paranoid Mode’ AI Agent Setup
summary: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has developed a privacy-focused setup for artificial intelligence agents that combines anonymous payments, encrypted network routing, and locally processed prompts, offering a glimpse of how AI services could operate without exposing users’ identities and personal...
content:
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has developed a privacy-focused setup for artificial intelligence agents that combines anonymous payments, encrypted network routing, and locally processed prompts, offering a glimpse of how AI services could operate without exposing users’ identities and personal information.

Key Takeaways

  • Buterin unveiled a privacy-focused AI agent setup combining Tor, zkAPI, and locally processed prompts to protect user identities.
  • Ethereum-based zkAPI enables anonymous AI payments using zero-knowledge proofs to conceal links between users and transactions.
  • Privacy challenges remain, including slow performance and potential network surveillance, prompting Buterin to explore stronger protections.

Buterin Goes ‘Paranoid Mode’ With Private AI Setup

In an X post Friday, Buterin described a new “paranoid mode” for his Pi AI agent harness, bringing together the Ethereum-based zkAPI payment system, the Tor anonymity network, random cover traffic, and a locally running large language model (LLM).

The experimental configuration is designed to address several ways AI services can identify users, including payment records, IP addresses, recognizable writing patterns, and the contents of submitted prompts.

Each conversation is assigned a separate Tor circuit, while additional randomized network traffic helps obscure genuine requests. Meanwhile, a local AI model rewrites prompts before forwarding them to external services, reducing the likelihood that identifying information reaches the provider.

Buterin said his implementation uses Qwen3.8-Flash-Next for local prompt processing, although the system allows users to substitute their preferred models. The privacy features are bundled into an OpenAI-compatible daemon, allowing them to operate alongside existing AI software.

Buterin also added another layer of security by running the Pi agent harness inside a Bubblewrap sandbox, which restricts its access to the surrounding operating system. The agent’s network connections are routed through Tor using torsocks, while Buterin said he’s experimenting with micro-virtual machines as an additional isolation mechanism.

The setup incorporates zkAPI, a privacy-preserving payment system launched Oct. 1 by the Ethereum Foundation and Open Anonymity Project.

As Bitcoin.com News previously reported, zkAPI uses zero-knowledge proofs to separate payment identities from individual AI requests. Users deposit cryptocurrency, including ETH or USDC, into an Ethereum-based vault and receive private credits that can be spent without linking each transaction to the original funding source.

The service issues temporary API credentials with spending limits, allowing customers to access AI models without maintaining conventional billing identities tied to their requests.

However, zkAPI alone does not provide complete anonymity. AI providers still receive the contents of prompts, while IP addresses, behavioral patterns, and other identifying details can potentially connect otherwise anonymous requests to individual users. Buterin’s latest experiment attempts to address those vulnerabilities by combining payment privacy with network anonymity and local processing.

Still Room for Improvement, Says Ethereum Founder

Despite the additional protections, Buterin acknowledged that his system remains imperfect.

“It’s getting quite usable!” he wrote, adding, “though you definitely still pay quite a bit in increased latency, especially when starting a new conversation.”

He also warned that Tor’s protections could be undermined by sophisticated adversaries. While randomized cover traffic can frustrate passive observers, an AI provider cooperating with a Tor entry relay could potentially manipulate request timing to identify users. Buterin suggested that a purpose-built mixnet, incorporating continuous cover traffic and greater bandwidth, could offer stronger protection against such attacks.

The Ethereum co-founder also said significantly cheaper gas costs for zkAPI deposits and withdrawals are coming to Ethereum mainnet, although he did not provide a timetable or specific figures.

The experiment highlights a growing intersection between cryptocurrency infrastructure and AI agents, demonstrating how blockchain-based payments, privacy networks and locally hosted models could work together to reduce the information exposed when interacting with increasingly powerful AI services.

Buterin’s privacy-centric setup also arrives just as AI giant OpenAI disclosed that an AI agent stole ETH on the Sepolia testnet from a wallet that it did not control—another potential risk with entrusting agents to handle crypto funds. The AI giant said it has implemented additional safeguards to try and prevent such incidents from happening again in the future.

title: Sazmining Now Sells Jack Dorsey’s Proto Immersion Hashboards
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Sazmining Now Sells Jack Dorsey’s Proto Immersion Hashboards 
Block’s Proto mining hashboards are now available on Sazmining’s mining-as-a-service platform. 
This post Sazmining Now Sells Jack Dorsey’s Proto Immersion Hashboards  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by...
content:
Bitcoin mining just got a lower barrier to entry. 

Sazmining announced Thursday that it is now selling Proto’s immersion hashboards directly to individual and institutional buyers through its mining-as-a-service platform. Previously, the hardware was mostly in the hands of large-scale operators.

Each hashboard delivers roughly 200 TH at around 15 J/TH, and buyers own them outright while Sazmining handles deployment, monitoring and maintenance at a US facility. Mining rewards go straight to the owner’s wallet.

The move follows a multi-megawatt supply deal between Sazmining and Proto — the bitcoin mining arm of Jack Dorsey’s Block (NYSE: XYZ) — which both companies expect to expand as demand grows.

“Because of our aligned-incentive model, Sazmining only earns when we produce bitcoin for our clients,” said Kent Halliburton, CEO and co-founder of Sazmining. 

He also pitched mining as a form of bitcoin acquisition diversification: rather than paying the market price on the day of purchase, a miner’s costs are spread across the machine’s working life.

Wyoming-based Sazmining, founded in 2018, operates renewable-powered facilities across the US, Paraguay, and Norway. It says its fleet runs more than 20 percentage points ahead of the Bitcoin network’s carbon-free share.

Proto is Jack Dorsey’s Block’s bitcoin mining play. The Twitter founder has spent years arguing bitcoin is the foundation of “a more open financial system,” funding everything from Cash App’s buy-and-send rails to the Bitkey self-custody wallet, and he framed mining as the obvious missing piece back in 2021: “Bitcoin mining should be as easy as plugging a rig into a power source.” 

Block formally announced it was building an open bitcoin mining system in January 2022, with the stated aim of making mining “more distributed and efficient.”

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, a new report highlighted substantial cost savings from stablecoin remittances, especially in emerging markets. Meanwhile, Solana postponed its Shanghai event after registrations exceeded local capacity limits and an OpenAI research model accessed a crypto wallet without authorization to deploy smart contracts.

Stablecoin remittances cost 84% less than traditional transfers, Borderless finds

Stablecoin-funded remittances cost roughly 84% less than traditional money transfers, according to a new third-quarter report from payments network Borderless.xyz.

Sending $200 through stablecoin payment networks costs a median of $2, or 1%, compared with $12.72, or 6.36%, for conventional remittances. The comparison uses Borderless pricing from the third quarter of 2026 and World Bank data from the same period last year.

Savings were particularly pronounced in emerging markets. In Sub-Saharan Africa, stablecoin remittances cost 2.9%, compared with 8.46% for traditional transfers. In Latin America, the respective costs were 1.25% and 5.64%.

Businesses also stand to benefit. A $10,000 stablecoin-funded transfer to the eurozone costs as little as $26, compared with $135 to $150 for an international bank wire, including foreign-exchange costs.

Stablecoin payouts also settled faster in several markets, with a median of two minutes in Brazil and Colombia and three minutes in Mexico. Traditional SWIFT transfers typically settled the next business day.

However, reliability varied. Payment completion rates reached 98.6% in Mexico but fell to 73% in Costa Rica, highlighting differences in local payment infrastructure.

Solana’s Liu says Shanghai event postponed over registration surge

The Solana Accelerate event in Shanghai was postponed after pre-registration exceeded the event cap set by local authorities, according to Lily Liu, president of the Solana Foundation.

Event registration quadrupled overnight following publicity for the event, Liu wrote in a Friday X post, adding that organizers decided to postpone the event to “comply with local requirements.”

Earlier on Friday, X users claimed that the event was “abruptly suspended” as law enforcement officers were stationed at the venue.

In October 2025, a Solana event in Shenzhen was also cut short due to venue capacity and public-safety concerns, Solana’s Chinese-language community account announced then on X.

Shanghai was scheduled to open Solana’s four-city Accelerate China tour, followed by Hangzhou on Sunday, Shenzhen on Tuesday and Beijing on Thursday, according to the event’s website.

The postponement followed Solana executives’ promotion of a new Shanghai office earlier this week.

OpenAI model helped itself to testnet crypto, then kept quiet about it

An internal research model at OpenAI accessed a funded crypto wallet without authorization, using testnet Ether to deploy smart contracts on the Sepolia network and later omitting the spending from its final task summary. 

OpenAI said the model, which was part of its GPT-5.6 Sol family, was given the task of updating a crypto trading prototype and deploying compatible contracts. After failing to obtain testnet ETH through faucets, the model derived accounts from publicly known developer recovery phrases, checked 362 wallet addresses and selected one with enough funds to proceed. 

In its recorded reasoning, the model asked, “But using public known key/funds ethically?” It then argued that the funds were “effectively abandoned/test ETH” and that Sepolia ETH had no value, before using the wallet’s private key to sign and broadcast a deployment transaction. The transaction succeeded, with fees charged to the account.

OpenAI said the incident showed how an AI model could decide on its own that using someone else’s funds was acceptable, even without permission. The company discovered the incident while reviewing earlier model activity and has since introduced safeguards to prevent live internet access in similar situations.

title: Taiwan Blocks Coinbase and Kalshi Over Bets on Its November Elections
summary: Taiwan has blocked the websites of Coinbase and Kalshi under a court order sought by police investigating election betting, six weeks before the island’s Nov. 28 local elections. Kalshi’s own member agreement already bars Taiwanese users, yet it lists markets on the races. A Criminal Court Order Six...
content:
Taiwan has blocked the websites of Coinbase and Kalshi under a court order sought by police investigating election betting, six weeks before the island’s Nov. 28 local elections. Kalshi’s own member agreement already bars Taiwanese users, yet it lists markets on the races.

Key Takeaways

  • A New Taipei court order cites Taiwan’s election law, under which operators face up to five years in prison.
  • Kalshi lists Taiwan as a restricted jurisdiction but runs a Taipei mayor market with about 198,000 contracts.

A Criminal Court Order Six Weeks Before the Vote

Coinbase’s website has been unreachable in Taiwan since Oct. 14, when users began seeing a block page that cites a criminal ruling by the New Taipei District Court under the Public Officials Election and Recall Act, according to tests by Taiwanese crypto outlet BlockTempo. The court authorized Taiwan’s telecoms regulator and internet registry to block both Coinbase and the prediction market Kalshi, Bloomberg reported on Oct. 15.

Taiwan’s Criminal Investigation Bureau, which sought the order, told Bloomberg it requested the restrictions to protect election integrity and prevent “overseas interference,” without giving further details. Authorities have separately warned that money from mainland China could flow into the island ahead of the vote, though they have not accused Coinbase or Kalshi of handling funds from China.

A Coinbase spokesperson told Bloomberg the company is aware of access issues for some users in Taiwan and is investigating. Under a 2023 amendment to the law, people who bet on elections face up to six months in prison and gambling operators up to five years.

Meanwhile, a Kalshi spokesperson told Bloomberg the company doesn’t allow trading in Taiwan, and its member agreement lists Taiwan among the “Restricted Jurisdictions” whose residents may not use the platform. Even so, the exchange lists markets on the Nov. 28 vote.

On its Taipei mayoral market, about 198,000 contracts had traded by Friday, with Chiang Wan-an at 58 cents and Shen Bo-yang at 39 cents. Kalshi also lists the New Taipei and Kaohsiung mayoral races, whether the Kuomintang will win the most mayoral and magistrate races, and the 2028 presidential election. BlockTempo noted that Coinbase’s Kalshi-powered predictions product shows the presidential market, though it called any link to the block speculation.

Taiwan first blocked Polymarket’s domain in December 2023 and blocked it again in May; that block page cited a Miaoli District Court ruling under the same law. Polymarket still lists about two dozen markets on Taiwan’s local races, and its Taipei mayoral market has seen about 1.14 million shares traded.

Prosecutors have also gone after individual Polymarket bettors, tracing them through onchain flows, BlockTempo reported on Oct. 2. In Kaohsiung, a court sentenced a man to 30 days detention after he bet 742.96 USDC on which party would win the most seats, netting about NT$102, and his USDC was confiscated. In Tainan, a bettor on the Taipei mayoral race received a deferred prosecution on condition of paying NT$100,000 to the state treasury.

Taiwan’s crackdown follows Indonesia’s block of Polymarket over bets on its president and South Korea’s pursuit of users, where police traced Polymarket bettors through the blockchain.

title: Hot Inflation Data Puts Bitcoin Under Pressure, but ‘Difficult’ Isn’t ‘Bearish’: CoinShares
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Hot Inflation Data Puts Bitcoin Under Pressure, but ‘Difficult’ Isn’t ‘Bearish’: CoinShares
Bitcoin is still reacting to weekly data but long-term investors shouldn’t be worried, according to the European asset manager. 
This post Hot Inflation Data Puts Bitcoin Under Pressure, but...
content:
Bitcoin’s price has dropped this week as new inflation data has come in hot. 

But while the largest cryptocurrency’s near-term setup is difficult, it’s not “fundamentally bearish,” according to European asset manager CoinShares’ Head of Research, James Butterfill. 

In a report Friday, the analyst said that bitcoin’s near-term challenge stems from a macro environment that’s caught in an awkward middle ground: inflation is too elevated for the Fed to ease up, while the economy is too resilient to force a policy pivot. 

“Bitcoin and the broader digital asset market have moved lower on the resulting hawkish repricing, a reminder of how sensitive Bitcoin remains to monetary policy over short horizons,” he wrote. 

Bitcoin’s price recently stood at $81,473, down 2% over a seven-day period. 

The price of the leading cryptocurrency dropped Wednesday after data showed that U.S. consumer prices shot up more than expected in September. 

Then, on Thursday, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said that U.S. producer prices rose in September at the fastest pace in more than four years. 

This has weighed on bitcoin’s price because higher inflation means the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates. Higher borrowing costs can restrict the liquidity the digital coin needs to rally. 

The Federal Reserve hiked rates in September and will meet at the end of this month. 

But Butterfill added that investors should be patient and advised investors to instead think in the long-term and not react to any single weekly data point. 

“For investors, that argues for reading the coming weeks as a data-driven range rather than a trend, and for sizing digital asset exposure against a strategic allocation rather than against this week’s print,” he wrote. 

Bitcoin spent the first half of 2026 in a bear market but had its best quarter in years after surging in August and September. Analysts have now said the leading cryptocurrency is now back in a bull market after trading above its 365-day moving average. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Canada Tightens Prediction Market Rules, Banning Brokers from Displaying Sports Contracts
summary:
Canadian brokers offering event contracts must now keep markets they cannot offer out of clients’ sight, not just block trades in them. 
The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) has extended its restrictions to how prediction markets appear in broker apps and promotions.
London's tradi...
content:
2026-10-16T20:01:00.000+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 18:01 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Canadian brokers must keep ineligible event contracts out of search results, recommendations and marketing, even when trading is blocked.
  • Wealthsimple’s promotional page still shows hypothetical OpenAI IPO and Apple product questions.

Canadian brokers offering event contracts must now keep markets they cannot offer out of clients’ sight, not just block trades in them.

The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) has extended its restrictions to how prediction markets appear in broker apps and promotions.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The updated requirements, published on 16 October, also explicitly prohibit sports and entertainment contracts. Brokers distributing products from US prediction exchanges will therefore need a separate Canadian selection of markets.

Brokers Must Filter the Entire Product Experience

CIRO says dealers must keep unavailable contracts out of search results, recommendations and marketing, even when clients cannot trade them. Sending clients to those markets through links to third-party sites is also prohibited.

The regulator says showing such contracts could give clients the impression that they are authorised in Canada. A broker connected to a larger US exchange must therefore filter markets before they reach its Canadian interface.

The rule may also affect how brokers advertise prediction markets.

Wealthsimple’s Predict page still displays illustrative questions about an OpenAI IPO and a foldable Apple phone. Those examples do not mean the contracts are available to trade, but Wealthsimple may need to review whether they can remain in Canadian-facing marketing.

Economic and Financial Contracts Remain Available

CIRO continues to permit selected contracts tied to economic data, environmental measurements and financial indicators. Eligibility depends on an objective way to determine the outcome, such as an official statistic or a recognised market benchmark.

The existing minimum maturity of 30 days and prohibition on leverage also remain in place. CIRO set out those conditions in its earlier guidance.

CIRO had already said in August that sports and entertainment contracts did not belong within the securities-regulated offering it authorised for dealers. The latest notice makes the restriction explicit and extends it to the way those markets are presented to clients.

Two Brokers Currently Serve the Canadian Market

Interactive Brokers Canada launched event contracts in April 2025, and became the first dealer authorised to offer those products in the country. Its Forecast Contracts trade through ForecastEx, the CFTC-regulated exchange owned by Interactive Brokers.

Wealthsimple later received authorisation and now distributes selected Kalshi contracts through its separate Predict app. Its Canadian offering is limited to approved financial, economic and climate-related markets.

As ForecastEx and Kalshi add contracts, both brokers will have to assess each new market before it enters their Canadian product feeds. Keeping an ineligible contract off the trading screen is no longer enough if clients can still encounter it elsewhere.

title: Crypto PACs escalate spending against Sherrod Brown in Ohio Senate race
summary: At least two industry-aligned PACs have poured more than $52 million into opposing Sherrod Brown’s return to the Senate.
content:
Affiliates of the Fairshake political action committee (PAC), largely funded by Coinbase and Ripple Labs, have increased their initially announced expenditures by more than 50% in what could be a key race for control of Congress in 2026.

According to Thursday filings with the Federal Election Commission (FEC), the Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs — a group that supports Republican candidates in primaries and elections — spent $46.6 million on media opposing former lawmaker Sherrod Brown and supporting Republican incumbent Jon Husted in Ohio’s Senate race for the 2026 midterms. The spending marked a sharp increase over what Fairshake said in September it initially planned to spend opposing Brown’s return to the Senate: $30 million.

“I’ve spent my career taking on Wall Street, taking on big pharma, taking on big oil and been successful in many cases,” said Brown in an interview aired Friday on Pod Save America, addressing the attack ads funded by the crypto industry, adding:

“Jon Husted is their boy [...] They know he’s their guy, they know I’m going to hold him accountable and I guess it’s a perfect storm, so they spend literally tens and tens of millions of dollars.”

With just under three weeks until the US election, early voting has already been underway for 10 days in Ohio. Notably, Fairshake’s affiliate was not the only crypto-aligned PAC to ramp up spending as Ohio voters cast their ballots. The Digital Freedom Fund, a Super PAC created by Gemini co-founders Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss, reported about $3 million in ad spending this week to oppose Brown and support Husted, bringing the group’s total media purchases in the Ohio race to more than $5.9 million.

Fairshake’s expenditures have already exceeded its efforts in 2024, when the PAC spent $41 million supporting Republican Bernie Moreno and opposing Brown, who was running for reelection to the Senate at the time. The Democratic lawmaker chaired the Senate Banking Committee and was one of the more outspoken voices challenging laws and policies favored by the crypto industry while serving in Congress.

Related: Vivek Ramaswamy’s gubernatorial run lacks the crypto rhetoric of his presidential bid

The Ohio race isn’t Fairshake’s only focus with the midterm elections looming. Defend American Jobs reported spending more than $6.7 million to oppose Independent candidate Dan Osborn in Nebraska’s Senate race. Osborn is running against Republican Pete Ricketts, who voted in favor of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act and the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act while in office.

Cointelegraph reached out to Fairshake and Husted’s campaign for comment but did not receive an immediate response.

How could the 2026 elections shape US crypto laws and policy?

Fairshake has been open about its intention to “back pro-crypto candidates” in 2026 as part of a goal to fill the next session of Congress with lawmakers supportive of policies favored by the industry. The PAC reported in January that it held $193 million in cash on hand ahead of the elections.

Beyond PACs like Fairshake and Digital Freedom Fund, other groups aligned with crypto interests have already tried to influence 2026 voters. The Fellowship committee, backed by Cantor Fitzgerald and Anchorage Digital, reported spending more than $11 million between August 2025 and August 2026, largely on media supporting House and Senate candidates.
