title: Quantum Alliance forms amid warnings 6.4 million bitcoin face future quantum threat
summary: Nine crypto companies launched the Quantum Alliance to jointly prepare for quantum attacks, but they disagree on when the threat will arrive and whether vulnerable BTC should be frozen.
content:
Oct 16, 2026, 6:52 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Experts warn that a future quantum computer could expose the secret keys of wallets holding an estimated 6.4 million bitcoin, including 1.1 million attributed to Satoshi Nakamoto, though no existing machine can do so.
  • Researchers disagree on when the threat could emerge, with one citing 2028 as realistic, while a new industry alliance is developing standards to help blockchains adopt quantum-resistant security.
  • Proposals to freeze, move or place vulnerable bitcoin in a trust have raised concerns about property rights and network neutrality, and any security upgrade would require broad coordination across the Bitcoin ecosystem.

Who gets Satoshi Nakamoto’s 1.1 million bitcoin, and, for that matter, millions more that are at risk if quantum computers become powerful enough to break the security protecting it, has been a topic of intense debate for quite some time.

Christopher Smith, CEO of quantum-resistant layer-1 blockchain Quantus, believes whoever develops that technology first could take those tokens worth billions, potentially with government backing.

“The most likely scenario is that whoever gets the first CRQC (Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer) will take them, probably with the blessing of whichever national government,” Smith told CoinDesk. “Hopefully it’s a government that likes bitcoin.”

The security researcher and protocol engineer’s warning comes as nine crypto companies unveiled the Quantum Alliance on Thursday to develop common security standards for bitcoin, Ethereum and other blockchain networks.

The concern is that future quantum computers could reverse-engineer a wallet’s publicly visible key to uncover its secret key, allowing attackers to steal funds. The Alliance estimates that 6.4 million bitcoin, or 30.2% of the supply, have public keys already exposed. Those coins, it clarified, cannot be stolen this way today because no existing quantum computer is yet powerful enough.

The first question many are asking today is when quantum computers will actually be a threat to bitcoin. Bryn Bennett, chief revenue officer at The Vault, responded: “Nobody knows the date, but the estimates keep falling, and the risk is one we can already plan for. The question for custodians isn’t whether the date is 2028 or 2035; it’s whether you can migrate in time if it arrives early.”

Richard Carback, chief technology officer of Postquant Labs, disagreed, saying he believes 2028 is a realistic date for a machine capable of breaking today’s cryptography.

Recent research has reduced estimates of the computing power needed to attack bitcoin and Ethereum. But no existing machine can break their cryptography, and predictions about when one might arrive remain disputed.

The prospect of those BTC tokens being stolen raises yet another difficult question: should developers freeze vulnerable assets, such as Bitcoin holdings, before quantum computers can reach them? Carback says he prefers that they be moved rather than frozen, while Bennet sees a different problem.

“Nobody owns that issue, and that’s the problem,” Bennett told CoinDesk. “A custodian protects its clients’ assets, not abandoned ones. Freezing coins is a governance decision for the Bitcoin network, not for the industry.”

“Any freeze would trade quantum risk for a precedent on property rights and neutrality,” he added.

The debate has been ongoing. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao suggested freezing Satoshi’s estimated 1.1 million bitcoin if the coins remain untouched as quantum technology advances. Bitcoin developer Jameson Lopp has also proposed restrictions on vulnerable coins to prevent future theft. But critics argue that freezing someone’s bitcoin goes against the promise that no one can confiscate it.

Making bitcoin quantum-resistant would mean replacing the digital signatures used to authorize transactions. That requires agreement among developers, miners, wallet providers, exchanges and users.

“Nobody has a credible single number, and anyone offering one is guessing,” Bennett said of the cost. “The real cost isn’t the cryptography; it’s coordinating wallets, exchanges, custodians and protocol developers.”

The replacement signatures could also take up more space on the blockchain, potentially increasing fees or reducing the number of transactions bitcoin can process. Researchers are already working on ways to limit that impact.

The Quantum Alliance, whose members include Hacken, Charles Hoskinson’s Midnight Foundation, Quantus and Postquant Labs, plans to publish common security tests and guidance for moving existing networks to quantum-resistant systems.

Carback also proposed placing vulnerable coins in a trust, allowing owners who can prove ownership to recover their funds. For bitcoin holders, the unresolved question is whether the network can protect their money without changing the rules that made the number one cryptocurrency so appealing in the first place.

title: Tokenized Tesla surges as Elon Musk unveils SpaceX-powered flying Roadster prototype
summary: Volume in Hyperliquid’s Tesla contract hit $47 million in one hour after Elon Musk’s flying Roadster demo, up from $2.8 million, with U.S. stocks closed.
content:
Summary

  • Trading in Hyperliquid’s Tesla contract rose from $2.8 million to $47 million in a single hour overnight. It is already the contract’s second-busiest day since launch.
  • The contract’s price rose about 5% to roughly $378. Binance’s Tesla contract was still the largest, with $279 million in 24-hour volume against Hyperliquid’s $159 million, according to RootData.
  • The contract tracks Tesla’s stock price but is not a tokenized share. It trades around the clock and allows up to 20x leverage.

Traders rushed into Tesla-linked crypto markets overnight after Elon Musk unveiled a flying version of the Roadster, with trading on Hyperliquid jumping while U.S. stock markets were closed.

The surge shows how crypto exchanges that never close are becoming the first place investors react to news about traditional companies.

Musk demonstrated the prototype, which uses SpaceX thruster technology, on Oct. 15, after Tesla TSLA$354.74·Market Closed shares closed at $362.44. Hyperliquid’s TSLA perpetual contract rose about 4.9% to roughly $378, and hourly trading volume leapt about 1,580%, from $2.8 million to $47 million.

It is already the contract’s second-busiest day since listing a year ago, with the daily candle only nine hours old. Binance remained the largest venue, with $279 million in 24-hour volume versus Hyperliquid’s $159 million, according to RootData, but Hyperliquid held the most open interest, at $99 million. Tesla shares were up about 4.5% in premarket trading.

Hyperliquid’s contract, listed through Trade.xyz, is a perpetual future that tracks Tesla’s stock price rather than a tokenized share. It settles in USDC, allows up to 20x leverage and requires no brokerage account. The contract trades around the clock, so it was one of the few ways to bet on Tesla’s price while Nasdaq was closed. Tesla is due to report third-quarter earnings on Oct. 21.

title: Altcoins outpace bitcoin as celestia jumps 16%, Warsh silent on interest-rate plans
summary: Celestia jumped 16%, injective rose 7.7% and layerzero added 7.3% while bitcoin held little changed near $82,100 and Fed Chair Warsh gave no sign on interest rates.
content:
Oct 16, 2026, 6:41 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • Bitcoin was little changed since midnight UTC near $82,100 after bouncing from a dip to about $81,600 at around 03:30 UTC.
  • Celestia jumped 16%, injective rose 7.7% and layerzero added 7.3%, leaving more than two-thirds of CoinDesk 100 members higher and the CoinDesk 5 flat.
  • Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal what the central bank will do later this month, and the odds of an October interest-rate increase fell to about 15% from almost 30%.

Bitcoin BTC$81,421.95 was little changed since midnight UTC, trading around $82,100 after bouncing from a dip to about $81,600 at around 03:30 UTC. It’s comfortably above Thursday’s brief break below $80,000, its first in a month.

Altcoins edged ahead, with ether ETH$2,417.25 adding 0.5% near $2,450 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) gaining 0.46%, while the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5) held steady. Celestia (TIA) jumped 16%, injective INJ$8.6926 rose 7.7% and layerzero ZRO$1.9535 added 7.3%, leaving four in every five CoinDesk 100 Index (CD100) members higher and lifting CoinMarketCap’s Altcoin Season index to 60 from 50 a day earlier.

Asian equities steadied after Thursday’s rout, with South Korea’s Kospi closing 2.05% higher and Japan’s Nikkei up 1.39%, while S&P 500 futures were little changed after the index snapped a three-day losing streak.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined to signal the central bank’s intentions for its meeting later this month in a speech at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, with the odds of an October interest-rate increase dropping to about 15% from roughly 30%, according to the CME Fedwatch tool. Treasury yields were largely stable.

Derivatives positioning

  • Trading volume cools, leverage resets: Crypto futures volume slid 20% over 24 hours to $200 billion, while open interest rose 2% to $142.21 billion. Liquidations dropped to $311 million from nearly $1 billion yesterday. Quieter trading with positions still building suggests the forced selling has run its course.
  • Sellers ease off: The 24-hour long/short taker volume ratio is balanced, compared with shorts making up 52% yesterday. Aggressive selling has faded.
  • BTC, ETH and SOL gains lack fresh long bets: Bitcoin's notional open interest rose just 0.3% against a 1% price gain, which means the number of contracts outstanding slipped slightly. Ether and solana show the same pattern, with open interest up by less than their spot prices. The moves look driven by traders closing shorts, not by new long positions.
  • XRP traders are cashing out into the rally: XRP's open interest fell 1% while its spot price gained 1.4%, so contracts were closed on a rise. Its 24-hour OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta, which tracks net aggressive buying and selling at market prices rather than passive limit orders, is also negative. The bounce has little support from derivatives traders.
  • ZEC leads with new bullish bets: ZEC futures open interest jumped 14% against an 11.5% price gain, so traders added contracts to the rise. Its OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta is the most positive among majors, a sign that buyers are the aggressors. TRX, XAUT and ETH also show positive readings while BTC is neutral and UNI, HBAR and XRP are negative.
  • Funding signals a bullish tilt but no froth: Annualized perpetual funding rates for major tokens hover between 5% and 10%. That shows a bias toward longs but nothing out of the ordinary, so the market is far from overheated and has room for further gains.
  • Implied volatility keeps falling: BVIV, the 30-day implied volatility index for bitcoin, slammed to 38% from yesterday's high of 42%, and ether's implied volatility also fell. Options traders are pricing a calmer market, which matches the funding picture.
  • Options traders hedge while eyeing ether upside: Decentralized exchange Derive pointed to a large bitcoin put spread that crossed the tape early this week, betting on a drop to $78,000. The $80,000 put is the most traded option on Deribit, the centralized options giant, so some traders are still buying downside protection. In ether, the $2,600 call is the most traded of the past 24 hours.

Token talk

  • Celestia (TIA), the modular data-availability network token, rose 16% to around $0.68, the biggest gain in the CD100 and a 2026 high. The token has advanced about 59% over four weeks, with the rally coinciding with Celestia Fibre hitting 3.07 terabits per second in a throughput benchmark and the introduction of a proposed economic upgrade called the Sustainable Blob Economy.
  • Injective INJ$8.6926, the finance-focused layer-1 token, climbed 7.7% to about $9.19. While there’s no obvious, overriding narrative, there are three pending U.S. exchange-traded fund applications tied to the token. CoinMarketCap shows $289.7 million of INJ volume over 24 hours, up 128% from the prior day.
  • LayerZero ZRO$1.9535, the cross-chain messaging token, gained 7.3% to about $2.24, extending a rally linked to its ATLAS trading infrastructure, which routes most of its fees into buying and burning the token. Ether.fi (ETHFI), the liquid restaking token, rose 4.2%.
  • Starknet STRK$0.07306 was the weakest CD100 member, down 9.6% to $0.08 after an 11% gain on Thursday, and stacks STX$0.3865, a bitcoin-staking layer token, fell 4.2%.
  • Larger names were mixed to higher, with solana (SOL) up 1.2% to about $107, XRP up 0.5% and monero (XMR) up 2.9% to about $565, while BNB barely moved.

Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 16, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its October 2026 Proof of Reserves (PoR) report. Independently audited by Hacken, the report confirms that the platform’s reserves continue to fully cover user holdings across all major reserve assets. As part of its commitment to putting users first, MEXC publishes monthly reserve data that users can independently verify, reinforcing user trust through transparency.

According to the audit report, MEXC’s reserve ratios stand at 294% for BTC, 122% for USDT, 115% for USDC and 111% for ETH. All four reserve ratios exceed the 100% benchmark, with BTC showing the largest margin above the benchmark.

MEXC’s PoR framework combines user-level verification, on-chain transparency, and independent third-party audits. Through Merkle Tree technology, users can independently verify that their account balances are included in the platform’s reported liabilities while preserving the privacy and confidentiality of user account information. MEXC also publicly discloses its custodial wallet addresses, enabling independent verification of its on-chain holdings. To further strengthen transparency and external oversight, MEXC partners with Hacken, an independent blockchain security and auditing firm, to conduct monthly Proof of Reserves audits covering Proof of Liabilities, Proof of Ownership, Reserves Calculation, and a Merkle-tree verification.

Beyond regular PoR reporting, MEXC continues to strengthen its multi-layered security framework to protect user assets. The platform employs cold and hot wallet management, supported by multi-signature authorization and layered risk controls. The MEXC Futures Insurance Fund helps cover losses that exceed a user’s margin following liquidation, providing a risk buffer during extreme market conditions. The Guardian Fund is designed to protect users facing serious security incidents, including large-scale exploits, targeted attacks, and unforeseen system vulnerabilities. Recent attacks across the digital asset industry have again demonstrated that security threats are not static.   • The fintech firm brings trading, risk management, client support, and Web3 payments together to support institutional growth across global markets.

UPTECH, a fintech firm providing institutional technology infrastructure for FX, CFD, and multi-asset brokerages, is marking its UF AWARDS APAC 2026 nomination by highlighting the integrated architecture behind its technology offering. The company views the nomination as industry recognition of its technical approach to helping financial institutions modernize operations and support growth.

For brokerage leaders, expansion requires more than additional trading capacity. Execution, risk oversight, client service, and payments must work together as operations become more complex. UPTECH addresses these requirements through a unified, modular ecosystem designed to reduce operational friction while giving institutions flexibility in how they develop their brokerage infrastructure.

Connecting core brokerage operations

The UPTECH ecosystem brings together five core products. CTOTrader provides a multi-asset trading platform solution, while UPBASE serves as an all-in-one web trading client platform. Together, they connect the trading environment with the client-facing experience within the broader infrastructure.

UPSHIELD adds enterprise risk management and on-chain anti-money laundering intelligence, placing risk oversight alongside the ecosystem’s trading and payment capabilities. UPTOPAY supports Web3 payments through a decentralized, multi-asset smart contract payment protocol. UPAGENT completes the offering with an intelligent helpdesk and ticket system for brokerage customer support.

By bringing these functions into an integrated architecture, UPTECH aims to reduce the complexity of coordinating disconnected systems. Its modular approach allows brokerages to align technology adoption with their operational priorities, with enterprise security and continuity central to the company’s infrastructure philosophy.

Supporting clients across the markets

For institutions serving Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, and Africa, a consistent client experience must also accommodate different languages and local market needs. UPTECH’s approach to AI-powered localization addresses this challenge through tools designed to help support teams respond in the languages their clients use.

Within UPAGENT, a Bring Your Own Key framework enables brokerages to connect their preferred large language models. Combined with custom knowledge bases, the system supports real-time, bidirectional translation tailored to local dialects, generates context-aware replies, and executes workflow actions in native languages. These capabilities help brokerages extend multilingual service without increasing local support staffing proportionally.

UPTECH’s focus is on applying fintech innovation to practical institutional requirements: coordinated operations, enterprise risk oversight, and responsive client service. The UF Awards nomination marks a milestone in that work as the company continues to position unified infrastructure as a foundation for brokerage growth.

summary: Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 16, 2026 — MEXC, a global cryptocurrency exchange, released its AI Trading Report, based on a survey of 3,708 crypto traders. The report examines how respondents use AI, how much trading authority they would delegate, and what protective measures they expect from platform...

Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 16, 2026 — MEXC, a global cryptocurrency exchange, released its AI Trading Report, based on a survey of 3,708 crypto traders. The report examines how respondents use AI, how much trading authority they would delegate, and what protective measures they expect from platforms. Blockchain security firm Hacken contributed technical analysis of risks associated with AI agent trading and the controls designed to address them.

Key takeaways:

  • 84.8% of surveyed crypto users have used AI for research or trading. While 58.3% report improved market research, 46% also report better trade execution, though 54% have yet to see improvement at the execution stage.
  • Interest in AI agents is already significant: half of respondents are interested in AI agents but have not tried them. 
  • 65.9% of AI users act on its advice at least sometimes; only 20% have tried execution without approving each trade.
  • 54% would let AI trade with some funds, but no more than 20% of their account; only 6.5% would authorize more than half.
  • Half of users with automated execution experience worry they could fail to detect or stop problems in time.
  • Willingness to use automated trading grows from 55% under the baseline scenario to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage and losses are added.
  • 95.5% support at least one mandatory protective measure, even as many want control over their own settings.

The report found that 84.8% of respondents had used AI to analyze or trade digital assets in the previous six months, with 53.1% using it at least weekly. Adoption was higher among younger participants: 88.5% of respondents aged 18–34 had used AI, compared with 69.9% of those aged 45 and older. Among respondents who reported not using AI, difficulty getting started or high entry barriers was a more common obstacle than AI mistrust, cited by 46.7% and 32.7%, respectively.

AI’s biggest role remained preparation before a trade. Summarizing news was among the most frequent tasks for 54.3% of AI users, ahead of market analysis at 48.6% and finding trading opportunities at 38%. Only 7.6% selected direct execution as one of their most-used tasks. Looking at their most recent AI-assisted trade, 68.9% said AI contributed most before execution, compared with 22.7% during trading.

Users were also more positive about research than execution. While 58.3% reported better market research, 46% reported improved execution. Another 30.9% saw no change in execution, and 23.1% said it had worsened. These assessments reflect respondents’ experiences rather than independently measured trading performance.

AI advice nevertheless influenced trading activity. Among AI users, 65.9% said they placed orders or adjusted positions based on its recommendations at least sometimes. These groups could overlap.

Risk limits changed respondents’ willingness to automate. In a scenario offering notifications, pausing and permission revocation, 55% were willing to let AI trade automatically. Adding limits on funds, assets, positions, leverage and losses, with automatic stopping at the loss threshold, brought willingness to 71.8% — an increase of 16.8 percentage points.

That willingness did not extend to most of an account’s funds. In a separate scenario prohibiting transfers and withdrawals and allowing users to stop trading at any time, 54% would authorize no more than 20% of their account assets and only 6.5% would authorize more than half.

Hacken’s contribution examines why withdrawal restrictions alone cannot prevent losses. An agent with trading access could still be manipulated into buying an asset at an inflated price or taking on excessive exposure. Its analysis outlines protective measures set independently of the agent, including limits on orders, total positions and permissions, alongside security testing to ensure unwanted actions are blocked before execution.

On oversight, 46.2% of respondents preferred exchanges to offer safety settings users could choose to enable, about 1.8 times the share who preferred uniform minimum requirements set by the platform (25.7%). Support for user choice did not mean rejecting industry standards: among those who preferred optional settings and answered the separate standards question, 97.8% backed at least one mandatory measure.

Across all 3,464 valid responses to the standards question, a risk assessment or knowledge test before first use received the most support at 55.3%. Independent audits and limits on capital and loss that cannot be disabled followed at 38.8% each.

“As AI becomes more integrated into trading, our findings show that users don’t want less control. They want clearer boundaries,” said Vugar Usi Zade, CEO of MEXC. “For traders, that means clear risk limits, the ability to intervene when needed, and confidence that the platform has done its part before automation begins.”

The full AI Trading Report, including Hacken’s security contribution, is available here.

About MEXC

Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity.

title: Scammer gets scammed in Ledger spy-chip exploit, loses almost $5 million in bitcoin
summary: Chainalysis says a fraudster who tricked people through fake online jobs became one of the biggest victims of the compromised hardware wallets.
content:
Summary

  • A crypto scammer who made millions through fake online job offers lost more than $4.9 million in bitcoin after thieves compromised Ledger hardware wallets.
  • Chainalysis said the scammer transferred proceeds from their scheme to three wallet addresses, from which attackers stole 60 bitcoin.
  • The theft was linked to Ledger devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that contained unauthorized implants capable of transmitting wallet recovery information over a mobile network.

A crypto scammer who made millions tricking people by offering fake online jobs has fallen victim to another scam, losing bitcoin worth more than $4.9 million through compromised Ledger hardware wallets.

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said Thursday on X that the perpetrator had collected the bitcoin through a so-called task scam, in which people are initially paid to post fake product reviews or boost online sales. Then they are told their accounts have a negative balance and they must deposit their own money before they can withdraw their supposed earnings.

According to Chainalysis, the person behind the operation transferred the proceeds of the illegal activity to three Ledger wallet addresses, which thieves emptied, taking 60 BTC.

The incident adds a twist to the Ledger security breach involving devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. Investigators discovered unauthorized hardware implants capable of transmitting wallet recovery information over a mobile network, giving attackers access to the bitcoin stored on affected devices.

title: Zcash (ZEC) Price Prediction: Relief Rally Faces $1,288 Resistance as Head-and-Shoulders Pattern Signals Correction Risk
summary: Zcash (ZEC) has rebounded above $1,200 after a sharp correction from its September highs, but bearish chart patterns and overhead resistance continue to complicate its recovery prospects.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ZEC

Zcash (ZEC) has rebounded above $1,200 after a sharp correction from its September highs, but bearish chart patterns and overhead resistance continue to complicate its recovery prospects.

The Zcash price climbed toward $1,230 on October 16, 2026, after recently testing support near $1,077. Traders are now watching whether ZEC can extend its relief rally toward $1,288 or resume its decline toward lower support levels.

Zcash Price Prediction: $1,288 Resistance Puts Recovery to the Test

Zcash’s latest rebound follows a correction of approximately 34%–36% from highs near $1,700. The pullback has reduced some of the gains from its sharp rally, while leaving the token well above its longer-term moving average. Market data for October 16 showed Zcash closing near $1,231, with the 200-day moving average around $669.

The $1,200–$1,288 range represents a potential short-term rebound zone, aligning with descending trendline resistance and upper Fibonacci extensions. Source: Eric Van Tassel via X

Technical trader Eric Van Tassel identified a potential relief rally on the one-hour Coinbase chart, using Fibonacci retracement levels and a descending trendline to map possible upside targets. The analysis places the $1,200–$1,288 area in focus as a zone where the recovery could encounter renewed selling pressure.

The upper end of that range is consistent with independent technical readings. Montbon’s October 16 analysis placed its first resistance level near $1,290, while CoinCodex listed resistance around $1,235 and $1,326. These levels vary by methodology but collectively highlight the challenge facing ZEC as it attempts to recover.

A sustained move above $1,288 would strengthen the short-term recovery case, particularly if buyers can keep the price above reclaimed support. However, an intraday move through resistance would not, by itself, establish a lasting trend reversal. Traders would need to assess whether subsequent candles hold above the breakout area and whether buying activity supports the move.

Head-and-Shoulders Pattern Raises Downside Risks

The potential recovery is complicated by a head-and-shoulders formation identified by Eric Van Tassel on the four-hour ZEC/USD chart. The pattern consists of a left shoulder, a higher peak known as the head, and a right shoulder. It is generally considered bearish when price breaks below the neckline connecting the intervening lows.

ZEC’s continued rally without a meaningful correction could turn the head-and-shoulders pattern into a potential double top, although the H&S structure remains valid unless price breaks above the head. Source: Eric Van Tassel via X

Tassel’s chart analysis identifies a possible downside target near the 0.618 Fibonacci retracement level around $727. That level represents a projected scenario rather than a confirmed destination. The pattern’s significance depends on how the price develops, particularly whether ZEC breaks below the neckline and confirms the bearish structure.

The trader also cautioned that a renewed advance without a meaningful pullback could weaken the head-and-shoulders interpretation or produce a different structure, such as a double top. This distinction matters because chart patterns are conditional signals, not guarantees of future price direction.

The Zcash price was rejected at the 4-hour downtrend line and $1,229 horizontal resistance, forming another lower high and potentially exposing support at $1,080–$1,059. Source: @AstroCryptoGuru via X

A separate four-hour analysis from AstroCryptoGuru identified a bearish rejection near the descending trendline and horizontal resistance at $1,229. The trader interpreted the move as another lower high and highlighted potential downside levels at $1,080 and $1,059. Those levels are considerably closer to the current price than the $727 Fibonacci projection and therefore represent separate stages in the bearish scenario.

Ichimoku Cloud Signals Possible Retest Near $879

MaisonCypher’s daily-chart analysis offers another perspective on Zcash’s correction. The trader noted that the price had moved above the upper boundary of the Ichimoku Cloud before turning lower toward the cloud’s lower boundary. The indicator helps traders assess trend direction, momentum, and potential support or resistance zones.

ZEC could briefly dip toward $879 to reset momentum indicators, with holding cloud support critical to establishing a reversal base for a potential medium-term recovery. Source: @MaisonCypher via X

MaisonCypher highlighted approximately $879 as a possible downside level if the correction continues. The analysis suggests that a move toward this area could help reset short-term momentum indicators before another attempt at recovery. However, the price would need to stabilize around relevant support for that scenario to develop.

The $879 level also sits well below the more immediate support areas identified by other traders. ZEC’s ability to defend the $1,080–$1,059 zone could therefore be important in determining whether selling pressure remains contained or develops into a deeper retracement.

Independent market indicators show a mixed picture. On October 16, Zcash’s daily relative strength index (RSI) stood around 47, while its MACD remained negative, according to Montbon’s technical analysis. The RSI reading suggests that momentum was neither strongly bullish nor deeply oversold, while the negative MACD points to lingering weakness.

These readings do not rule out a rebound, but they offer limited confirmation that buyers have regained control. The Ichimoku Cloud’s lower boundary, the $1,080–$1,059 support region, and the nearby resistance zone remain important reference points for the next phase of price action.

ZEC Price Prediction: Key Levels to Watch

Zcash’s short-term outlook depends on whether the latest rebound can overcome resistance or whether sellers regain control near the descending trendline.

On the upside, $1,229–$1,288 forms the immediate resistance area highlighted by the supplied chart analyses. A sustained breakout above this zone could open the way toward higher resistance, although confirmation would depend on follow-through buying and the ability to hold reclaimed levels.

Zcash (ZEC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

On the downside, $1,080 and $1,059 are the first notable support levels identified by AstroCryptoGuru. A decisive break below this region could expose Zcash to further losses. The $879 level represents a deeper correction scenario from MaisonCypher, while XRPathologist’s $727 projection is tied to the potential completion of the head-and-shoulders pattern.

These targets should not be treated as a single forecast. They reflect different chart structures, timeframes, and assumptions. The head-and-shoulders pattern would carry greater weight if ZEC breaks its neckline, while a sustained move above resistance could undermine the bearish setup.

Macro and Asset Outlook

Zcash’s broader market context remains relevant to its price outlook. The cryptocurrency uses zero-knowledge cryptography to support shielded transactions, giving it a distinct position among digital assets. However, its technological characteristics do not prevent sharp price swings or guarantee continued demand during periods of market weakness.

ZEC’s advance toward $1,700 earlier in the year was followed by a substantial retracement, illustrating the volatility that can accompany rapid price appreciation. Its position above the 200-day moving average suggests that the longer-term trend remained stronger than the immediate price action indicated, but shorter-term momentum was less convincing.

For now, the $1,288 resistance level represents an important test for the relief rally. A successful breakout could improve the short-term outlook, while another rejection may bring $1,080 and $1,059 back into focus. If those supports fail, the lower targets near $879 and $727 become relevant bearish scenarios.

The next directional move will depend on how the Zcash price responds at these technical levels. Until resistance is reclaimed or support breaks decisively, the price outlook remains divided between a recovery attempt and the risk of a deeper correction.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin dips to $81,000 as stocks slide, VIX soars ahead of Black Monday anniversary
summary: A Friday surge in oil prices hit already-shaky equity markets, sending the Nasdaq down more than 2%.
content:
coverage endedOct 16, 2026, 4:45 p.m. EDT

A Friday surge in oil prices hit already-shaky equity markets, sending the Nasdaq down more than 2%.

VIX soars, Nasdaq sheds 2% ahead of 39-year anniversary of 1987's Black Monday market crash

Surely just a coincidence, but this coming Monday marks the 39-year anniversary of the Black Monday, October 19, 1987, stock market crash, when the S&P 500 plunged more than 20%.

That makes today the 39-year anniversary of the Friday before the 1987 crash. While not nearly as dramatic as the S&P 500’s 5% decline 39 years ago, the Nasdaq fell 2.15% today.

Alongside, the volatility index (VIX) — often referred to as the “fear gauge” — soared 22%.

Rumors were flying of someone or some group getting blown out of their positions, but nothing’s been confirmed just yet.

Bitcoin is off of its lows, but still down 1% over the past 24 hours at $81,500.

Stocks losses quickly double, with bitcoin attempting to decouple

The Nasdaq is at session lows a bit less than 90 minutes before the close of trading for the week, down 2.3%. The S&P 500 is down 1.25%.

What was a modestly negative day appears to have turned into a rout as oil prices quickly jumped about $3 per barrel over the past couple of hours. WTI crude is now up 3.8% to $101.70.

Government bonds — which benefitted earlier this week as money flowed into fixed income alongside declining stocks — aren’t seeing a bid today. The 10-year Treasury yield is near the day’s high at 5.112%.

After initially declining alongside stocks earlier on Friday, bitcoin is attempting to stabilize as equities add to losses this afternoon. It’s currently at $81,350, down 1% over the past 24 hours.

Crypto stocks slammed as oil surges, interest rates turn higher, and stocks slide

Rising slowly at first, the price of oil is headed straight up over the past few minutes, with WTI crude now up more than 3% on the day to a one-month high of $101 per barrel.

That’s up 16% over the past 10 days.

There are reports that Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline has been targeted in an attack.

U.S. government bond yields are responding; the 10-year Treasury is now higher by 3.5 basis points to 5.125% after earlier dipping to 5.07%.

The Nasdaq is lower by 1.5% and bitcoin has pulled back to $81,300.

Among crypto-related stocks taking losses: Strategy MSTR$136.76·Market Closed -9.2%, Securitize (SECZ) -13.4%, Coinbase COIN$173.21·Market Closed -3.5%, Circle CRCL$82.25·Market Closed -4%, Bullish BLSH$29.48·Market Closed -5.9%.

Oil quietly hits one-month high

Down earlier in the session, front-month WTI crude oil has climbed to a one-month high of $99.40 per barrel, up 1.5% on the day, with much of the move coming in the past few minutes — though there’s no particular news that’s hit the tape.

The action may be spooking the bond market, where U.S. Treasury yields have swung from declines to gains over the past hour.

U.S. refined products (gasoline and distillates) inventories, meanwhile, continue at decade lows, according to government data.

The Nasdaq is near a session low, off 1.4% for the day.

Bitcoin remains in the $81,500 area.

Bitcoin turns lower as tech declines grow

After a volatile week of trading in stocks and bonds, Friday had gotten off to a slow start, but declines are speeding up late in the U.S. morning.

The Nasdaq is now down 1.2%, led by big drops in familiar AI-related names.

Among the Mag 7, Tesla has turned lower after opening with sizable gains following its Roadster event last night. Apple is the only gainer in the group, up 1.1%.

The selling is spreading to crypto, where bitcoin has dipped about 1% over the 30 minutes to $81,500.

Fixed income is catching a bid, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield now barely down for the day at 5.08% after earlier rising to 5.13%.

Bounce in neoclouds proves short-lived, with CoreWeave down 8%

After days of relentless selling, the neoclouds — former bitcoin miners turned data center providers to the fast-growing AI sector — bounced hard on Thursday, many closing the day in the green after early sharp declines.

The selling has resumed on Friday, though, with CoreWeave (CRWV) lower by 8% and extending its weekly decline to more than 20%.

Hut 8, IREN, CleanSpark, Keel Infrastructure, and Cipher Mining are all down roughly 6%.

In a note on Friday, Goldman Sachs pointed out that the widening in high-yield bond spreads is an AI story: Non-AI-related spreads were barely higher this week, while AI-related spreads widened by 25 basis points.

“We view AI-related corporate bonds, from either neoclouds or firms with significant frontier lab exposure, as being at the epicenter of the funding cost debate,” said the bank’s Amanda Lynam.

Anthropic asked to delay IPO by NYC comptroller

“I write to urge Anthropic to pause its planned initial public offering until the company fully and transparently addresses the artificial intelligence safety, governance, and development pace concerns it has raised,” wrote New York City Comptroller Mark Levine to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei this week.

Levine noted in the letter that as comptroller, he is an investment adviser, custodian, and trustee of NYC pension funds, with more than $325 billion in assets.

AI-related selloff continues in early Friday trading

The tech sector came back from the brink on Thursday, but selling has resumed in U.S. trading on Friday morning.

The Nasdaq is slumping 0.7% while the less-AI-focused S&P 500 is flat and the DJIA is rising 0.7%.

Micron, Intel, AMD, Dell, SanDisk, and KLA Tencor are among the names down 3%-5%.

Declines among the Mag 7 are more subdued, and Tesla is even rising slightly after its flying-car demonstration last night.

Bitcoin is trading quietly near $82,000, up 2% from 24 hours ago.

Strive raises $630 million with new preferred offering

Bitcoin treasury company Strive ASST$24.10·Market Closed upsized the offering of its new high-yielding preferred stock, SATS, to 7 million shares (from 5 million).

The sale was priced at $90 per share, giving the company gross proceeds of $630 million.

Press release here.

At $90, the effective yield on the 15% dividend-paying stock would be a whopping 16.67%.

Strategy declares conditional daily dividend for STRC to begin November 1

Led by Michael Saylor, the company announced weeks ago its plan to switch to a daily dividend (from monthly) for its high-yielding preferred stock STRC.

The change is subject to a shareholder vote, which is underway, and the results will be known on Oct. 28.

Today’s announcement is thus conditional on the vote being in favor of the move to daily payments.

While strongly rebounding from its panicky lows of early summer, STRC continues to trade just below par value (yesterday’s close was $99.53), leaving Saylor and team unable to raise bitcoin-buying capital by issuing more shares.

Warsh isn't ruling out October rate hike, but markets mostly have

“I don’t prejudge meetings,” said Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at a fireside chat overnight at an IMF event. “I don’t believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings we have."

“It’s a new chapter at the Fed, and we’re not in that business anymore.”

Warsh defended the September rate hike as a necessary move to cool inflation.

He said the AI boom was the most important thing happening to global economies now, and said it was likely creating price pressures. Productivity gains will come, he said, but the road will be bumpy.

Rates are modestly higher from yesterday’s close, the 10-year U.S. yield up 2.9 basis points to 5.12%.

October Fed rate hikes odds have dipped to 15% from nearly 45% in the moments after the CPI report on Wednesday.

Crypto selloff after inflation report is temporary, Binance's Catherine Chen says

The latest inflation-driven crypto selloff is a short-term reaction rather than a sign of deeper trouble, according to Catherine Chen, Binance's head of institutional.

“The CPI-driven selloff is a sentiment shock, not a structural break,” Chen said, referring to the Consumer Price Index, a measure of U.S. inflation.

Chen expects inflation to peak around October, with clearer signs of cooling potentially emerging in March 2027. Lower energy prices and easing inflation could eventually help crypto markets recover, she said.

“A difficult trading day does not determine the outlook for the next several months,” Chen added. “The window for relief may already be approaching.”

ZEC jumps 11% even as its ETF loses $15 million

Bitcoin climbed back above $82,000 on Friday, a day after a brief drop under $80,000, as ZEC led a broad crypto bounce with an 11% jump to about $1,230 — even as investors pulled money from the token’s only U.S. ETF.

SOL and ether each gained more than 3%, to about $106 and $2,450, and DOGE and XRP added between 2% and 3%. BNB, HYPE and TRX rose about 1%, and bitcoin was up nearly 1%, according to CoinDesk data.

The bounce hasn’t reached the ETFs. The U.S. spot ZEC fund lost about $15 million on Thursday, its fifth outflow this month, according to SoSoValue data. Ether funds shed about $60 million, and SOL funds lost nearly $10 million, their ninth straight day of withdrawals. XRP funds saw a small outflow.

Bitcoin ETFs drew a net $5 million, a thin inflow after Wednesday’s $261 million exit.

A second straight day of bitcoin ETF inflows would be the first sign the bounce from $80,000 has buyers behind it.

title: The Markets Are Closed, but Over-the-Counter Trading Continues Through the Weekend: Is Your Brokerage Risk-Ready?
summary:
For many FX and CFD brokers, the close of the trading week does not close the risk.
Exposure built up during the week stays on the book over the weekend, and some OTC and alternative instruments continue to trade after conventional markets have shut. Developments outside normal hours can move prices...
content:
2026-10-16T11:46:09.015+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 09:46 GMT by tapaas

Disclaimer

  • Weekend liquidity thins as institutional participation drops, yet exposure stays on the book and some instruments keep trading. For FX and CFD brokers, that makes real-time visibility matter most when the market looks quietest.

For many FX and CFD brokers, the close of the trading week does not close the risk.

Exposure built up during the week stays on the book over the weekend, and some OTC and alternative instruments continue to trade after conventional markets have shut. Developments outside normal hours can move prices before liquidity returns on Monday. The market can look quiet without the broker’s risk going quiet with it.

That gap matters more as brokerage infrastructure becomes faster and more automated. A position that looks manageable at Friday’s close can look very different once liquidity thins, spreads widen or an unexpected event reprices the market. For dealing desks and risk managers, the question is not only where the book stands when markets close, but how that exposure could behave while conditions keep changing.

Why weekend liquidity changes the risk picture

During active sessions, deep liquidity and continuous participation keep pricing and execution relatively stable. As major institutional participants step back and conventional markets close, that depth falls away.

Thinner liquidity can widen spreads, increase slippage and produce sharper moves when new information hits a quiet market. The reopening can add gap risk, as prices adjust to everything that happened while venues were closed. For a broker carrying weekend exposure, the relevant question is not simply whether a client is holding a position, but what that position represents against the wider book, the state of liquidity and how clients are behaving.

A static end-of-day report cannot answer that on its own.

The blind spot in end-of-week reporting

Risk assessed mainly through retrospective reporting leaves a gap. A report produced after the fact can establish what happened; it cannot tell a dealing desk what is building in the book while conditions are still moving.

Weekend risk rarely comes from a single large position or one sudden move. It tends to build from several smaller changes at once: exposure concentrating in one direction, liquidity deteriorating, unusual client activity, or a pricing condition that leaves the broker more exposed than its headline numbers suggest. Seen separately, and after a delay, each looks minor. Seen together, and in real time, they form a picture a broker can act on.

Real-time risk intelligence when the market slows

This is where Tapaas positions its real-time risk intelligence platform. It is a layer rather than a trading system: it sits above a broker’s existing platforms, bridges and liquidity providers, connecting to them and consolidating their data into a single real-time environment.

From there, it tracks exposure, open positions and profit and loss across all books continuously, so risk and dealing teams work from one live view instead of waiting on separate reports. Its trader surveillance monitors client activity as it happens, flagging irregularities and high-risk behaviour, while its liquidity monitoring analyses slippage, fill rates and liquidity-provider performance in real time.

The reopening can add gap risk, as prices adjust to everything that happened while venues were closed. title: Your Bourse and 4XPORTAL Go Public With Broker Technology Tie-Up Aimed at Dubai
summary:
Your Bourse, a liquidity technology provider, and CRM vendor 4XPORTAL said today (Friday) they jointly serve forex brokers. About two to three brokers use the combined setup, Your Bourse told FinanceMagnates.com.
So far the focus has been FX and CFD brokers in 4XPORTAL's Dubai network, including Ind...
content:
2026-10-16T11:30:00.000+02:00

Friday, 16/10/2026 | 09:30 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Talks began late last year, and two to three brokers have used the combined setup since about April.
  • No joint package comes with it, and the CRM vendor stays the main contact for clients in its hub.

Your Bourse, a liquidity technology provider, and CRM vendor 4XPORTAL said today (Friday) they jointly serve forex brokers. About two to three brokers use the combined setup, Your Bourse told FinanceMagnates.com.

So far the focus has been FX and CFD brokers in 4XPORTAL's Dubai network, including Indian brokers that operate there. Pepperstone opened a Dubai hub after approval from the Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA) as retail broker interest in the emirate grew.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Talks between the two firms began in late 2025. The partnership took operational shape around April, according to Your Bourse, and the announcement describes an arrangement that already supports active clients rather than a new product.

For brokers in 4XPORTAL's hub, the arrangement means Your Bourse's pricing, liquidity and risk tools come through the vendor that already runs their CRM . The companies pitch the setup at brokers that would otherwise buy client systems and trading technology from separate providers.

Two to three users compare with the more than 100 clients 4XPORTAL lists on its website.

Other Vendors Sell Both Halves

Spotware has assembled a comparable offer through a package that puts Intivion's AltimaCRM alongside its cTrader platform and cBridge liquidity bridge.

Match-Trade keeps both halves inside one group. Its Match-Prime Liquidity arm started operating in December 2020 under a license from the Cyprus Securities and Exchange Commission (CySEC).

Your Bourse has used the same model before. In September 2025 it announced a tie-up with B2BROKER, which sells back-office software and trading platforms to brokers.

That deal gave B2BROKER clients access to Your Bourse's trading engines, liquidity aggregators and risk tools, according to the two companies.

No Joint Package, One Main Contact

No joint package is being launched. 4XPORTAL remains the main operational contact for clients in its hub, Your Bourse said, adding that it was still confirming how contracts are split between the two firms.

Adnan Khan, CEO of 4XPORTAL, said the partnership gives brokers "a more connected technology setup across their client operations and trading environment."

4XPORTAL's side covers the ATARIA CRM, payment services, know-your-customer and anti-money laundering checks, and custom software work.

Your Bourse, founded in 2017 and based in Limassol, handles pricing, liquidity connections, trade routing and risk controls. Axi adopted its matching engine, liquidity aggregation and risk tools in May 2025.

Two months later, Axi relaunched AxiPrime as an institutional liquidity service on the same technology.

title: ChangeNOW Announces NOW AI After Resolving Website Integration Vulnerability
summary: Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 15th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, 15th October 2026, Chainwire

Kingstown, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, October 15th, 2026, Chainwire

On October 15, with the help of independent security researchers, we found a vulnerability affecting one of the integrations used on the ChangeNOW website. The vulnerability has now been fixed.

We currently have no evidence that it was exploited. But we also can’t assume that the researchers who reported it were the only ones to find it. Because of that, we’re looking at the different possible scenarios and warning clients about the information that could potentially have been exposed. This may include email addresses and transaction details.

Please note ChangeNOW’s transaction infrastructure was not affected, and customer funds were never at risk.

The main thing clients should watch out for now is suspicious or fraudulent messages. A phony message could reference real transactions or support to appear legitimate. If you get an unexpected message that looks like it’s from ChangeNOW, please check the sender before responding, clicking on any links or giving any information. We exclusively contact clients via [email protected] and we will never ask for a private key, seed phrase, or any password by email.

People contact our support and compliance teams because they trust us with information they would not share publicly, and we understand the responsibility that comes with that. We have no indication this vulnerability was exploited, but we believe it is important to warn of the possible risks rather than wait until there is total certainty.

Our clients are at the center of what we do, and we’re continuing to upgrade the protection of our products. One of the actions we are taking is the launch of NOW AI, a dedicated protection lab with a mission to raise the security standard across all ChangeNOW products. We want to apply the same technology to the defensive side to spot danger earlier and bake stronger security into our products, especially as AI makes malicious action easier to automate and expand.

Today’s case only made the need to move faster more obvious and it accelerated the launch of NOW AI. We’ll publish more details on our plans, what it covers, and how it will be used across ChangeNOW on a dedicated page on our website soon. Stay tuned.

About ChangeNOW

ChangeNOW.io is a crypto super app built for every crypto move, giving newcomers, professionals, and businesses the tools they need to access Web3 finance in a simple and secure way.

Since 2017, ChangeNOW has grown from a fast, secure, and limitless instant exchange into a trusted platform where storage, swaps, trading, staking, and asset management are covered in one simple experience for millions of clients worldwide.

title: Orbs – DeFi’s Next Big Users Are Banks and Bots
summary: Ran Hammer is CEO at Orbs, a decentralized Layer-3 blockchain that works behind the scenes for DEXs. It gives smart contracts the automation and execution logic they lack on their own, which powers limit orders, TWAP, liquidity aggregation and perpetual futures across dozens of venues. Ran is an Isr...
content:
Skip to content

Ran Hammer is CEO at Orbs, a decentralized Layer-3 blockchain that works behind the scenes for DEXs. It gives smart contracts the automation and execution logic they lack on their own, which powers limit orders, TWAP, liquidity aggregation and perpetual futures across dozens of venues. Ran is an Israeli based in London and a former high-tech M&A lawyer. He has been with Orbs since its 2017 beginnings, working as general counsel, then in business development, then as chief business officer, before taking over as CEO in September.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Ran came to crypto the way many lawyers of his generation did. In 2015 a university friend and future Orbs co-founder, Daniel Peled, told him he had raised money for his startup in Bitcoin. Within two years Ran was the rare attorney at a reputable firm who understood the technology, and he spent the 2017 ICO boom advising clients who wanted to do things by the book when no book existed yet. Nine years into Orbs, he explains plainly what the project is: a proof-of-stake network with no TVL or DEXs of its own, which supplies the automation and logic that smart contracts can’t perform by themselves. That makes Orbs nearly invisible to the traders who use it. Ran is candid that this is good for users and difficult for a project whose token benefits from retail recognition. He also acknowledges that the market has moved enough that a small pivot is needed for Orbs to stay relevant.

His view of the current market is sober. The yield chasing of DeFi summer has mostly gone. Many retail traders left after the October 10, 2025 liquidation cascade and did not return. The activity that remains is increasingly professional, ranging from two-person trading teams running bots to BlackRock buying spot assets for its ETFs, which is why Ran prefers the term “on-chain finance.” He calls Hyperliquid the most successful dApp to date. He also argues that most DEXs, even ones that dominate their ecosystems, cannot build Hyperliquid-level order book depth. Orbs’ answer is Perpetual Hub Ultra 2.0, an intent-based model in which hedgers take the other side of trades and offset them across Binance, Hyperliquid, Lighter, Variational, Aster and other venues. Users get pairs from all of those markets on whatever chain they’re on, with a single collateral. QuickSwap has already made it the default perps engine across its chains.

Ran says he rarely opens Google or Gmail anymore. He runs most of his online life through a Telegram bot on OpenClaw, with Anthropic and OpenAI models working in loops. That habit led Orbs to repackage its products as an MCP and an agent skill, and to think seriously about how a protocol gets discovered when an AI agent, rather than a person, chooses which tools to use. He says the Orbs swap skill now outranks bigger, better-funded projects on adoption, while noting that actual agentic trading volume is still smaller than the hype suggests. He also covers the recently passed OIP-9 DAO vote, upcoming Season 1 tokenomics built on revenue-funded buybacks and burns, and record staking levels despite a token he openly says is underpriced. In the hot take round, Ran calls himself 80 percent Bitcoin maximalist. He predicts that within ten years banks will provide liquidity and trade through AMMs instead of OTC desks, and says most people still underestimate what today’s AI tools can do.

VIENNA, October 15, 2026 – BingX EU (MEGE zweite GmbH) has secured its Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA or MiCAR) license from Austria’s Financial Market Authority (FMA), that will enable the platform to offer regulated crypto services across 29 countries of the European Economic Area (EEA), subject to ongoing passporting arrangements. The authorization marks a significant milestone in BingX’s European expansion, providing EEA users with access to digital asset services under a unified regulatory framework built on transparency, security, and investor protection.

The authorization reflects BingX EU’s long-term commitment to responsible growth in Europe. As digital assets become increasingly integrated into the financial system, regulatory clarity plays an essential role in strengthening user confidence, supporting institutional participation, and enabling sustainable industry development. Through its regulated European entity, BingX EU will provide compliant crypto services designed to meet the evolving needs of both retail and institutional users across the EEA.

“Our priority is to provide European users with trusted and locally regulated trading experience,” said Daniel Lai, Chief Executive Officer of BingX EU. “Operating under MiCAR will allow us to deliver our services under a clear regulatory framework that gives users confidence while supporting the long-term development of Europe’s digital ecosystem. It also enables us to combine innovation with the high standards of security, transparency and accountability that European users and institutions expect. We believe this foundation can help create a more accessible and sustainable environment for the continued adoption of digital assets across the region.”

Looking forward, BingX EU will continue working closely with Austria’s FMA and other European regulators as it prepares for the launch of its regulated services across the European Economic Area. BingX EU remains committed to operating within Europe’s regulatory framework while providing users with secure, transparent and compliant access to digital asset services.

About BingX EU

MEGE zweite GmbH (“BingX EU“) is a MiCAR-regulated crypto-asset platform, headquartered in Vienna, licensed as a Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCAR). Dedicated to serving clients across 29 countries in the European Economic Area, BingX EU delivers fully regulated services in alignment with European standards for investor protection and market integrity. Under its MiCAR authorization, BingX EU provides a platform that offers regulated broker services, such as crypto custody, exchange, and other crypto services.

Founded in 2018, BingX is one of the the world’s leading multi-asset trading platform, serving more than 40 million users worldwide. The company has been the Principal Partner of Chelsea FC since 2024 and became the Official Team Partner of Scuderia Ferrari HP in 2026.

title: Polygon Unlocks 48-State US Payments Reach With Coinme and 4 Early OMS Customers
summary:
Key Takeaways: Polygon acquired Coinme, which expands its payments business to include coverage in the 48 U.S. states. Now it has 37 money transmitter licenses, 11 state exemptions and is
The post Polygon Unlocks 48-State US Payments Reach With Coinme and 4 Early OMS Customers appeared first on Cryp...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Polygon acquired Coinme, which expands its payments business to include coverage in the 48 U.S. states.
  • Now it has 37 money transmitter licenses, 11 state exemptions and is FinCEN registered.
  • First companies making payments, payroll and dollar access on Polygon Open Money Stack include Tazapay, Mesh, Toku & Kira.

Polygon Labs has completed its acquisition of Coinme, turning Polygon Open Money Stack into a regulated U.S. payments platform with direct links between fiat and onchain money movement.

The partnership provides Polygon with added protection and wallets, on-ramps, and cross-chain routing and settlement capabilities to shield its stablecoin payments.

  • Coinme Gives Polygon Coverage Across 48 US States
  • Stablecoins Connect More Directly to Local Currency
    • Mesh, Toku and Kira Expand Polygon’s Payments Footprint
    • Polygon Pushes Deeper Into Stablecoin Payments

Coinme Gives Polygon Coverage Across 48 US States

Coinme is Polygon’s U.S. payments service now available in 48 states, with 37 state money transmitter licenses and 11 exemptions that apply. The business is also registered as a money services business with FinCEN.

This regulatory component is being incorporated into the Polygon Open Money Stack (OMS).

It will aim to link bank accounts, cards and cash to onchain transfers, wallets and finally payouts. Businesses don’t need to stitch small transactions together from various providers; instead, they can send money into crypto rails with one stack, send money across networks, and then take it back down and make it usable as money in the real world.

Read More: Securitize Puts 12 U.S. Stocks on Solana With 1:1 Backing and 24/7 Trading Plans

Stablecoins Connect More Directly to Local Currency

Tazapay is amongst the early adopters of the OMS. It supports over 1,000 businesses and fintechs in more than 30 countries and has implemented Polygon’s on/off ramp solutions to reduce the time to market of stablecoins and local currencies.

The aim is to shorten the path for cross-border payments, without eliminating pre-existing local payment systems and SWIFT.

Mesh, Toku and Kira Expand Polygon’s Payments Footprint

Polygon OMS on-ramps will be added to the network cleared of over 300 wallets, exchanges and financial services. This integration provides alternative pathways between digital and fiat currencies without forcing companies to create numerous unique integrations.

Toku’s global payroll solutions are powered by Polygon wallets and payout systems. It handles local payroll, tax withholding and hiring compliance in over 100 countries, while also facilitating payments to employees who receive stablecoins and then use them to buy local currency.

Kira is also working to include Polygon OMS to increase the numbers of fintechs and institutional access to stablecoins. It has a platform that allows conversion to USD, ACH, Fedwire, FedNow, SWIFT and stablecoin. Kira 10 says the sign up takes only 72 hours and 9/10 payments are instant approval.

Polygon Pushes Deeper Into Stablecoin Payments

Coinme’s deal will take Polygon off the infrastructure-only business. Enabling regulated fiat entry into the application alongside on-chain settlement, wallets, and payouts, Polygon is developing one of crypto’s surging use-cases: transporting stablecoins from traditional financial systems to crypto networks.

Polygon OMS is in production now with its first customer demonstrating its ability to enable cross-border payments, account funding, payroll enrollment and access to the U.S. dollar.

title: VanEck Pulls Lido Staked Ethereum ETF After 1 Year, Ending stETH Fund Plan
summary:
Key Takeaways: VanEck has suggested to the Securities and Exchange Commission that it remove its proposed Lido Staked ETH registration. The S-1 was filed for the first time on October
The post VanEck Pulls Lido Staked Ethereum ETF After 1 Year, Ending stETH Fund Plan appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • VanEck has suggested to the Securities and Exchange Commission that it remove its proposed Lido Staked ETH registration.
  • The S-1 was filed for the first time on October 16, 2025 but not made effective.
  • No ETF shares were issued or sold and VanEck did not provide reasons for dropping the stETH cryptocurrency.

VanEck has officially put on the brakes on a long-anticipated U.S. exchange-traded fund (ETF) pegged to Lido staked Ether, concluding months of speculation in the cryptocurrency sector.

The asset manager filed a withdrawal request with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 14, 2026, confirming that it no longer intends to distribute shares of the proposed fund.

  • VanEck Withdraws Lido Staked Ethereum ETF Filing
  • No Shares Were Ever Issued
    • stETH ETF Plan Ends Without Replacement
    • Withdrawal Narrows VanEck’s Ethereum ETF Push

VanEck Withdraws Lido Staked Ethereum ETF Filing

VanEck Digital Assets filed a Form RW with the SEC that sought to withdraw the registration statement for the VanEck Lido Staked Ethereum ETF. The original Form S-1 was filed on October 16, 2025 under registration file number 333-290918 and was later amended.

VanEck indicated in a new filing that it withdrew its plans because the sponsor plans to not enter into the distribution of units of the trust.

The company didn’t specify what prompted the decision, which could have been due to regulatory concerns, market conditions, product strategy or something else.

Read More: Ethereum Hegotá Upgrade Puts 2 EIPs at Center of 62-Proposal Crypto Shakeup

No Shares Were Ever Issued

VanEck confirmed that it did not make the registration statement effective. It also stated that there was no distribution of any securities or a preliminary prospectus for the registration statement. That implies that the withdrawal ends the filing process prior to such product coming to the investors.

The new ETF was intended to sit at a stake position which is Lido’s own liquid staker protocol’s version of Ether, stETH, providing a secondary exposure to deposited ETH.

As a result of stETH being staked ETH and showing the accumulated staking rewards, the product offered was not exactly a traditional spot Ether ETF holding a position in ETH.

stETH ETF Plan Ends Without Replacement

VanEck didn’t state a successor fund or disclose if it plans to develop another Ethereum product focused on staking. The filing only states that the sponsor no longer plans to move forward with the existing trust. That leaves the prospects of VanEck’s Ethereum bet hanging in the balance.

Staking-based crypto ETFs have achieved attention due to their potential price exposure along with staking returns, whilst including more complexities upon the custody, rewards, liquidity and regulatory treatment.

Withdrawal Narrows VanEck’s Ethereum ETF Push

Another theme in the cancelled filing is the difference between traditional spot Ethereum exposure and investments over liquid staking tokens.

A stETH-based vehicle would have added another layer between investors and ETH itself, as stETH would be a claim relative to our staked ETH through Lido. But for now, VanEck has cut the route off.

The investors will not be able to access the planned Lido Staked Ethereum ETF via the structure originally proposed in the October 2025 edition.
